statements.title: A free field with two independent parameters
statements.text: Over \(\mathbb C\), let \(\kappa,\lambda\in\mathbb C\) and give \(V=\mathbb C[x_1,x_2,\ldots]\), \(Tx_r=rx_{r+1}\), the Wick contraction \(P(u)=\kappa u^{-2}+\lambda u^{-1}\). Its exchange satisfies \(S(u)(x_1\otimes x_1)=x_1\otimes x_1-2\lambda u^{-1}1\otimes1\), and its ordinary unital geometric point modules with all marked collisions are exactly the smooth modules with \([J_m,J_n]=(\kappa m\delta_{m+n,0}+\lambda\varepsilon(m)\delta_{m+n,-1})1\), where \(\varepsilon(m)=1\) for \(m\ge0\) and \(-1\) otherwise. The curved dual has zero differential and curvature \(\sum_{r\ge1}(\kappa r e_r+\lambda e_{r-1})e_{-r}\) on exterior cochains completed by finite negative-mode cutoffs separately in each exterior degree, with finite positive-mode support at each cutoff. For any two contractions of this form, the primitive field map \(V_{P+Q}\to V_P\otimes V_Q\) preserves fields and exchange and adds the contraction parameters; it is not a fixed-level fusion coproduct.

statements.title: Fock modules and rational coinvariants
statements.text: Over \(\mathbb C\) at \(\kappa\ne0\), consider Heisenberg modules with \([a_m,a_n]=m\kappa\delta_{m+n,0}\), each positive mode locally nilpotent, and sufficiently high positive modes annihilating each vector. The assignment \(E\mapsto\mathcal F(E)=E[x_1,x_2,\ldots]\), with \(a_{-m}=x_m\), \(a_m=m\kappa\partial_{x_m}\) and \(a_0=A_E\), is an exact equivalence from \(\mathbb C[a_0]\)-modules, and negative-current coinvariants recover \(E\). At finitely many distinct complex points, the derived coinvariants of the algebraic tensor product of these Fock modules under rational currents vanishing at infinity are \(\bigotimes_iE_i\) in degree zero. For finite-dimensional \(E_i\), their coinvariant connection is \(d+\kappa^{-1}\sum_{i<j}A_iA_j\,d\log(p_i-p_j)\); on scalar-charge dual fibres the positive half-exchange is \(e^{\pi i\alpha\beta/\kappa}\) followed by the flip, with normalized associator equal to one.

statements.title: Grading changes the derived endomorphisms
statements.text: For the algebraic Heisenberg mode algebra \(A_\kappa\) over \(\mathbb C\), with \(\kappa\ne0\), put \(\mathfrak n_-=\bigoplus_{m\ge1}\mathbb Ca_{-m}\), \(W=A_\kappa\otimes_{U(\mathfrak n_-)}\mathbb C\) and \(R=\mathbb C[a_0]\). With \(\deg a_n=n\), internally graded derived Hom, summed over internal degrees but retaining full products within each homogeneous component, gives a formal endomorphism dg algebra with value \(R\). In the ordinary unbounded derived category of all algebraic \(A_\kappa\)-modules, \(\operatorname{Ext}^0(W,W)=R\), \(\operatorname{Ext}^1(W,W)=(\prod_{m\ge1}V_m)/(\bigoplus_{m\ge1}V_m)\), where \(V_m=a_mR[a_m,a_{m+1},\ldots]\), and every other degree vanishes. For every polynomial Fock module \(\mathcal F(E)\), full \(\operatorname{RHom}(W,\mathcal F(E))\) vanishes, whereas derived negative-current coinvariants equal \(E[0]\).

statements.title: The Gaussian bulk and its boundary current
statements.text: On \(\mathbb C\times\mathbb R_{\ge0}\), take the Gaussian abelian Chern–Simons observable complex over \(\mathbb C\), with numerical \(k=\hbar\kappa\ne0\), pairing \(-\kappa(2\pi i)^{-1}\int\alpha\wedge\beta\), and boundary condition \(j^*\alpha\in dz\wedge\Omega_c^\bullet\). Its carrier is the direct sum over field number of completed projective bornological symmetric powers, realized by compact smooth kernels satisfying that boundary condition in every variable. The rotation-finite boundary cohomology is the universal rank-one Heisenberg vertex algebra \(V_k\), while interior cohomology is an exterior algebra on one degree-one class. With orientation \(dx\wedge dy\wedge dt\), the outward-oriented sphere operation and the generator \(\xi\) normalized by \(\iota_{J_0}\xi=1\), the bulk bracket is \(\{\xi,\xi\}=2\pi i/k\), and the corresponding finite-jet vacuum cohomology has algebraic secondary pairing \(1/k\).

statements.title: Vacuum extensions detect the Heisenberg level
statements.text: Over \(\mathbb C\) at \(\kappa\ne0\), restrict the polynomial Heisenberg Fock construction to finite-dimensional \(\mathbb C[t]\)-modules with nilpotent \(t\), where \(a_0=t\), and transport the product by \(\mathcal F(M)\star\mathcal F(N)=\mathcal F(M\otimes N)\). Prescribe the conformal-block connection \(d-(T_M\otimes T_N/\kappa)\,dz/z\) on these chosen coefficient spaces, with the ordinary associator; the positive half-exchange is \(\operatorname{flip}\exp(\pi iT_M\otimes T_N/\kappa)\). On the marked vacuum extension \(J=\mathbb C[t]/(t^2)\), with its inclusion and quotient maps \(i:\mathbb C\to J\), \(p:J\to\mathbb C\), normalized by \(i(1)=t\), \(p(1)=1\), \(p(t)=0\), and \(n=ip\), positive pure braid is \(1+(2\pi i/\kappa)n\otimes n\). A complex-linear exact strong braided equivalence preserving this exact marked extension and its unit identification between levels \(\kappa,\kappa'\ne0\) therefore requires \(\kappa=\kappa'\), although the ambient associative algebra \(\operatorname{RHom}_{\mathbb C[t]}(\mathbb C,\mathbb C)\simeq\Lambda(\epsilon)\), \(|\epsilon|=1\), is unchanged.

statements.title: A comparison preserving the vacuum and its operations
statements.text: For nonzero-level Heisenberg modules over \(\mathbb C\), construct an independently defined comparison between negative-current coinvariants and the degreewise completed curved cochain transform on one common localized category, preserving the marked vacuum, translation, rational collision maps and logarithmic transport. Extend the Gaussian endpoint construction to nilpotent vacuum extensions with compatible transport and framing: for two unit charges at level three, increasing-normal-coordinate graph transport around a positive full turn gives \(e^{-2\pi i/3}\), whereas positive Fock continuation gives \(e^{2\pi i/3}\). An opposite-transport functor or a comparison with the reverse braided target remains to be constructed, together with the comparison preserving mixed operations of independent local bulk observables. The outgoing collision normalization is taken on the positive-real branch in this phase test.

statements.title: Siegel–Weil for the hyperbolic genus
statements.text: Let \(V\) be a strongly rational holomorphic vertex operator algebra over \(\mathbb C\), with its conformal vector, algebraic graded direct-sum states, a chosen Cartan subalgebra of \(V_1\), strongly rational Heisenberg commutant \(C\), and associated positive-definite even lattice of rank \(r\ge3\). Write \(c=c(V)\), let \(\mathcal H(V)\) be its hyperbolic genus, let \(G_W\) be the finite image of the Cartan-preserving automorphisms of \(W\) on its associated lattice, and put \(m(V)=\sum_{[W]\in\mathcal H(V)}|G_W|^{-1}\). For \(r>4\) and \(\tau\) in the upper half-plane, \[\frac{1}{m(V)}\sum_{[W]\in\mathcal H(V)}\frac{\operatorname{ch}_W(\tau)}{|G_W|}=\sum_{\gamma\in\Gamma_\infty\backslash\operatorname{SL}_2(\mathbb Z)}\varepsilon(\gamma)^c\frac{\operatorname{ch}_C(\gamma\tau)}{\eta(\gamma\tau)^r},\qquad \Gamma_\infty=\{\pm T^n:n\in\mathbb Z\}.\] Here \(\eta\) is the Dedekind eta function and \(\varepsilon\) its standard multiplier, with metaplectic lifts when required; the sum is absolutely and locally uniformly convergent. At \(r=3,4\), multiply each summand by \(\operatorname{Im}(\gamma\tau)^t\), continue meromorphically from \(\operatorname{Re}t>1-r/4\), and evaluate at \(t=0\): the standard section specified by the real Gaussian and finite lattice-coset characteristic functions is regular there and has the same value, with the metaplectic convention at rank three. The proof uses the positive nonvacuum commutant weights supplied by Dong–Sun–Wang’s 2026 preprint; assuming those weights are strictly positive is an explicit alternative hypothesis. For this holomorphic class this establishes, in the absolutely convergent range \(r>4\), the character identity of Möller–Rayhaun, arXiv:2408.07117 (2024), Conjecture 5.7; at \(r=3,4\) the identity holds for the specified continuation. The arithmetic Siegel–Weil theorems are known inputs.
statements.antecedents: Möller–Rayhaun (2024), arXiv:2408.07117, Conjecture 5.7, Theorem 4.7 and Corollary 4.11; van Ekeren–Möller–Scheithauer (2015, preprint), Theorem 4.2; Dong–Sun–Wang (2026, preprint), arXiv:2611.12417, Theorem 3 and Corollary 5.3; Opitz (2018), Theorem 3.7.2; Kudla (2001, preprint), arXiv:math/0110236, Theorem 4.1(i) and Proposition 4.22.

statements.title: Characters, discriminant gluings and genus mass
statements.text: For a strongly rational holomorphic complex vertex operator algebra \(V\) with a chosen Cartan of \(V_1\), strongly rational Heisenberg commutant \(C\), positive-definite even associated lattice \(L\) of rank \(r\ge3\), and positive nonvacuum \(C\)-module weights as supplied by Dong–Sun–Wang (2026), put \(D=L^*/L\), let \(K\subset O(D)\) be the image of \(\operatorname{Aut}(C)\) on its simple modules under the opposite-discriminant identification, and set \(m_L=\sum_{[M]\in\operatorname{gen}(L)}|O(M)|^{-1}\). Every discriminant isometry \(\phi:D_M\to D\) gives the holomorphic extension \(W_{M,\phi}=\bigoplus_{a\in D_M}C_{\phi(a)}\otimes V_{M+a}\), on algebraic ordinary states, and the isomorphism classes over \(M\) are \(K\backslash\operatorname{Iso}(D_M,D)/O(M)\). For characters on the upper half-plane, let \(G_W\) be the full finite image of the Cartan-preserving automorphisms on the associated lattice, and set \(m(V)=\sum_{[W]\in\mathcal H(V)}|G_W|^{-1}\) over the hyperbolic genus. Then \[m(V)=\frac{|O(D)|}{|K|}m_L,\qquad \frac{1}{m(V)}\sum_{[W]}\frac{\operatorname{ch}_W}{|G_W|}=\eta^{-r}f^T\Theta_{\mathrm{av}},\qquad \Theta_{\mathrm{av}}=\frac{1}{m_L|O(D)|}\sum_{[M]}\frac{1}{|O(M)|}\sum_{\sigma\in O(D)}\sigma\theta_M,\] where \(f=(\operatorname{ch}_{C_a})_{a\in D}\) and \(\theta_M\) is the vector of lattice-coset theta series. The mass formula itself is known from Moriwaki and Möller–Rayhaun; the character contraction retains the entire discriminant symmetrization and the kernels of the lattice actions.
statements.antecedents: Moriwaki (2021, revised preprint), Theorem 4.16; Möller–Rayhaun (2024), Theorem 4.7, Corollary 4.11, Proposition 4.15 and Corollary 4.16; van Ekeren–Möller–Scheithauer (2015, preprint), Theorem 4.2; Dong–Sun–Wang (2026, preprint), Theorem 3 and Corollary 5.3.

statements.title: The hyperbolic average on marked curves in every genus
statements.text: Let \(V\), of central charge \(c=c(V)\), be strongly rational and holomorphic over \(\mathbb C\), with a chosen Cartan of \(V_1\), strongly rational Heisenberg commutant \(C\), associated positive-definite even lattice \(L\) of rank \(r\ge3\), and positive nonvacuum commutant weights supplied by Dong–Sun–Wang (2026), or assumed explicitly. For each \(g\ge1\), use ordinary algebraic modules, restricted duals, invariant forms with vacuum norm one, and a marked sphere with \(g\) disjoint paired handle sewings and an extra vacuum insertion. If \(B_g\) is the rank-one Heisenberg vacuum sewing series with constant term one, \(C_g\) the commutant vector built from its own creation and evaluation intertwiners, \(f_{C,g}=B_g^{-(c-r)}C_g\), and \(\Phi_{W,g}=B_g^{-c}Z_{W,g}\), then \[\frac{1}{m(V)}\sum_{[W]\in\mathcal H(V)}\frac{\Phi_{W,g}}{|G_W|}=f_{C,g}^T\Theta_{\mathrm{av}}^{(g)}=\kappa_{r,g}^{-1}f_{C,g}^TE_{D,g}(\Omega,0),\qquad \kappa_{r,g}=\begin{cases}1&r>g+1,\\2&r\le g+1.\end{cases}\] Here \(m(V)=\sum|G_W|^{-1}\) uses full effective lattice stabilizers, \(D=L^*/L\), and \(\Theta_{\mathrm{av}}^{(g)}\) is the mass-normalized lattice-genus theta vector symmetrized by one \(O(D)\)-element acting simultaneously on all handles. The Eisenstein vector uses the standard Gaussian and finite lattice-coset characteristic functions, parameter \(s=(r-g-1)/2+2t\), and continuation from \(r/2+2\operatorname{Re}t>g+1\); its value at zero is regular. Equality is coefficientwise in the finitely many plumbing parameters, locally analytic on disjoint-disc sewing domains, and continues as an equality of sections on marked smooth curves, compatibly with the actual geometric changes of coordinates, factorization and pinching, using the same VOA, lattice and gluing label on every component before averaging products. The commutant factor is defined on curve charts; only the theta factor is defined on full Siegel space. The arithmetic equality, including its factor, is known from Kudla at even rank and Li’s metaplectic theorem at odd rank.
statements.antecedents: Kudla, Some extensions of the Siegel–Weil formula (1992), Theorem I.2; Li (2023, revised preprint), arXiv:2110.07457, Theorem 2.2.9 and Remark 2.2.12; Damiolini–Gibney–Tarasca (2019, preprint), Theorem 8.5.1; Gui (2023, revised preprint), Theorem 13.1; Tuite–Welby (2023, preprint), equations (99)–(104), (114)–(115), (133) and §7.2; Carpi–Codogni (2026, preprint), Theorems 7.3–7.4 and Proposition 7.6; Dong–Sun–Wang (2026, preprint), Theorem 3 and Corollary 5.3.

statements.title: Averaging does not preserve scalar sewing products
statements.text: For the positive-definite even unimodular rank-sixteen genus \(\{E_8\oplus E_8,D_{16}^{+}\}\), let \(p=286/691\), \(q=405/691\) be the normalized inverse-orthogonal-group weights and write \(A_g=p\theta_{E_8\oplus E_8}^{(g)}+q\theta_{D_{16}^{+}}^{(g)}\), \(\Delta_g=\theta_{E_8\oplus E_8}^{(g)}-\theta_{D_{16}^{+}}^{(g)}\). On a block diagonal in Siegel space, \[A_{g+h}\big|_{g+h\to g,h}-A_gA_h=pq\Delta_g\Delta_h.\] The \(4+4\) restriction has nonzero coefficient \(3085190905724928000/477481\), detected by the ordered \(D_4\) Gram coefficients \(7257600\) and \(2096640\). For actual lattice-VOA curve amplitudes, with the same vacuum plumbing factor removed and a common determinant-line trivialization, the corresponding \(5+5\) separating coefficient is \(759006325862823886848000/477481\). The valid average retains the same lattice label on both factors before summing; scalar multiplication of separately averaged amplitudes fails.
statements.antecedents: Gaberdiel–Volpato (2009), equations (2.15)–(2.17), §3.1, equation (3.5) and §4; Carpi–Codogni (2026, preprint), Theorem 7.4 and Remark 7.5. The covariance identity is elementary.

statements.title: The masses of the rank-four genus with weight-one algebra of type C
statements.text: For the strongly rational holomorphic complex vertex operator algebra of central charge \(24\) whose weight-one Lie algebra is of type \(C_4\) at affine level \(10\), the associated lattice is \(\sqrt{10}D_4\). Its lattice-genus mass is \(1/1152\), and its hyperbolic-VOA-genus mass, using full effective Cartan-preserving lattice groups, is \(1/384\): \(|O(D_4)|=1152\), \(|W(C_4)|=384\), and the discriminant index is three.
statements.antecedents: Betsumiya–Lam–Shimakura (2022, preprint), §5.10, Propositions 5.28–5.29; Möller–Rayhaun (2024), Table 2. Orthogonal and Weyl group orders are standard.

statements.title: The rank-four character
statements.text: For the strongly rational holomorphic complex vertex operator algebra of central charge \(24\) with weight-one Lie algebra of type \(C_4\) at level \(10\), strongly rational Cartan Heisenberg commutant and associated lattice \(\sqrt{10}D_4\), the normalized hyperbolic-genus character average is \[j(\tau)-708=q^{-1}+36+196884q+21493760q^2+\cdots,\qquad q=e^{2\pi i\tau}.\] The genus has a single holomorphic isomorphism class.
statements.antecedents: van Ekeren–Möller–Scheithauer (2015, preprint), Theorem 8.1; Betsumiya–Lam–Shimakura (2022, preprint), Proposition 5.29; the standard central-charge-24 modular-character argument; Kudla (2001, preprint), Theorem 4.1(i).

statements.title: A coefficient-native category of charged endpoints
statements.text: For the Gaussian charged-endpoint construction, a chosen propagator defines a bounded dg product \(B_P\) on the compact smooth native carrier. The finite-free singleton coefficient category has all bounded \(B_P\)-linear maps, strict composition and units, balanced tensor and finite charged duals satisfying both triangles. Collar and moment functors are quasi-equivalences at this singleton scope. A specified continuous product bar contracts by a conjugated Euler homotopy, and smooth position families carry the actual differential-form correction. Separately, ordinary tensor descends in the split module-homotopy category, the polynomial tower has all-arity units on every dg \(E\)-module, and polynomial Wick maps have transported-operator corrections on the stated large-separation Laurent domain. These are coefficient and module-homotopy comparisons: the charged graded-free kernel remains non-\(K\)-flat in the ordinary derived category. Two compact sources of charges \(q,-q\) in one ball give a concrete failure of the naive all-position map to one energy-completed multipole point. Other recipients remain possible. The later point-derived local-cohomology coring and all-charge hybrid diagonal coring are specified separately below. The polynomial/pro factorizing marked-category system now carries the actual native cut actor, its higher cut and collision coherences, and both occupied-vacuum placements on the full ordered atlas. The common completed collision/separation carrier, supported lattice, nonsplit geometric left endpoint, invariant geometric balanced coring and physical sewing retain their stronger comparison requirements.

statements.title: Point-derived duality and the separate all-charge coring
statements.text: For the specified exterior-point and polynomial oscillator coefficient algebras, the genuine ordinary derived adjunction has kernel \(R\Gamma_{(t)}B\), \(B=k[t]\), with an explicit Čech counit, coproduct, idempotence and triangle identities. Its image is the \(t\)-power-supported derived sector. A separate hybrid coefficient enhancement admits every algebraic unbounded charged complex and all graded module-linear maps, with the diagonal Koszul coring and balanced triangles. The charged graded-free kernel remains non-K-flat over the exterior algebra; its ordinary and derived tensors are different. The full oscillator algebra has an actual derived unit roof. The product-bar homotopy has total-count bounds on the stated polynomial, fixed-field native and oscillator-energy domains; an arbitrary completion mixing infinitely many counts in one coefficient needs a further estimate. Finite independent point tensors retain these constructions. Collision-chart gluing, the geometric transverse actor and its balanced coring remain separate.

statements.title: Finite separated Wick maps and chosen primitive transport
statements.text: On the reduced exterior algebra over the fully separated configuration space, the explicit strictly unital \(A_\infty\) automorphism has arity at most the number of positions, a finite inverse, and finite insertions for arbitrary commuting charge matrices, including Jordan blocks, with all coefficient morphisms. A prescribed comparison is matched only under the stated relative, normalized-bar and complete universal formal Maurer–Cartan class hypotheses; this does not produce every numerical or supported relative homotopy. Absolute spectral identities use rational-kernel jet substitutions before expansion into one common Laurent domain. The strict Wick representative has no continuous extension from the full normal Taylor energy product to the specified finite-pole target. Other representatives and completions are not excluded. A chosen interior primitive difference gives bounded conjugations of the coefficient actions, full morphism composition and finite duals; specified additive choices compose strictly. Boundary restrictions, arbitrary-choice independence and physical sewing remain open.

rows.name: Affine Kac–Moody algebras at irrational shifted level
rows.summary: Universal affine algebras have curved mode duality, algebraic induction, supported fusion and KZ structures. For \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\), irrational native line parameter \(k\) and raw level \(-k-2\), the actual ordinary unit is an equivalence on every unbounded source under the stated native action, adjunction, affine-free-lift and cutoff hypotheses. The regular binary geometric comparison is an equivalence on smooth outputs whose cohomology is jointly locally nilpotent for the positive currents. General incoming completions, collision assembly and the independent physical boundary functor require further comparisons.

statements.title: The raw-level curved point dual
statements.text: Let \(\mathfrak g\) be a finite-dimensional simple complex Lie algebra with invariant form \(B\) normalized by long-root square two, and let \(\kappa=k+h^\vee\notin\mathbb Q\). For the universal affine algebra at raw level \(k\), the curved point dual is \((C^\bullet_{\mathrm{cont}}(\mathfrak g((z))),d_{\mathrm{CE}},+\eta_k)\), where \(\eta_k(xz^m,yz^n)=kmB(x,y)\delta_{m+n,0}\) and \(d\alpha(x,y)=-\alpha([x,y])\). Complete separately in each exterior degree by finite subsets of \(z^{-1}\mathfrak g[z^{-1}]\), allowing finite \(\mathfrak g[[z]]\)-dual support separately for each such subset, with no product over exterior degrees. This is the point dual for the universal envelope, rather than a formula for simple quotients or an identification with the affine vertex algebra at the complementary level.

statements.title: KZ fusion with an explicit collision comparison
statements.text: For a finite-dimensional simple complex \(\mathfrak g\), long-root square two and \(\kappa=k+h^\vee\notin\mathbb Q\), induce \(\mathbb V^k(E)\) from finite-dimensional \(\mathfrak g\)-modules \(E\), with positive currents acting trivially on the top. Their fixed-level product is \(\mathbb V^k(E)\odot\mathbb V^k(F)=\mathbb V^k(E\otimes F)\), with energy completion \(\prod_hX_{[h]}\), associator \(\Phi_{\mathrm{KZ}}(-\Omega_{12}/\kappa,-\Omega_{23}/\kappa)\), and upper-half-plane vertex braiding \(\operatorname{flip}\,e^{\pi i\Omega/\kappa}\), where \(\Omega\) is the Casimir tensor of \(B\). The rational-current Chevalley–Eilenberg collision map from distinct points to the completed one-point product is a quasi-isomorphism on modules with a finite Weyl filtration and finite-dimensional tops. The comparison extends to bounded-above complexes in that exact category by completing each term before direct-sum totalization; the completed target need not itself have finite support.

statements.title: An affine endomorphism obstruction
statements.text: Over \(\mathbb C\), use algebraic Laurent-polynomial \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) modes at any raw level \(k\), with \([e,f]=h\), \((e,f)=1\) and \((h,h)=2\), and put \(W_k=A_k\otimes_{U(z^{-1}\mathfrak{sl}_2[z^{-1}])}\mathbb C\). In full algebraic Chevalley–Eilenberg cochains computing ordinary \(\operatorname{RHom}_{A_k}(W_k,W_k)\), the degree-one cochain sending \(f_{-1}\) to the induced vacuum and every other negative basis mode to zero represents a nonzero class at every \(k\). Consequently this endomorphism dg algebra cannot be quasi-isomorphic to \(U(\mathfrak{sl}_2)^{\mathrm{op}}\) concentrated in degree zero, including at irrational shifted level. This assertion uses algebraic modes and full Hom; it does not replace the coinvariant construction of the KZ connection.

statements.title: A commutative noncritical vacuum model
statements.text: For a finite-dimensional simple complex \(\mathfrak g\), with long roots of square two, and any \(k\ne-h^\vee\), let \(V^k(\mathfrak g)\) be the universal vacuum and use continuous finite-jet cochains. The inclusion \(C^\bullet_{\mathrm{cont}}(\mathfrak g[[z]];\mathbb C)\to C^\bullet_{\mathrm{cont}}(\mathfrak g[[z]];V^k(\mathfrak g))\) is a dg vertex quasi-isomorphism with commutative source, and vacuum self-Ext in discrete smooth modules is \(H^\bullet(\mathfrak g;\mathbb C)\). It supplies a commutative \(E_3\)-model; uniqueness among all \(E_3\)-structures with this cohomology holds for \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) but fails for general simple \(\mathfrak g\), already for \(\mathfrak{sl}_3\).

statements.title: The nonabelian physical comparison
statements.text: For complex simple \(\mathfrak g\) at noncritical level, construct the boundary-module functor from an independently defined Chern–Simons theory and compare its supported insertions with affine rational-current collision maps. The comparison must preserve the universal vacuum, level normalization, horizontal transport and mixed bulk/boundary operations. Extend the algebraic collision comparison beyond finite Weyl filtrations only after identifying a module category and completion on which all iterated products are defined.

statements.title: Vacuum composition at every invariant level
statements.text: Let \(\mathfrak g\) be a finite-dimensional complex Lie algebra, \(B\) an invariant symmetric form, and \(s\in\mathbb C\). Put \(\ell=-sB-\operatorname{Kill}_{\mathfrak g}/2\). The affine vacuum cochain algebra \(A_s\) has a filtered multiplicative comparison \(A_s\simeq R\operatorname{End}^{\mathrm{wt}}_{U_\ell}(V_\ell)^{\mathrm{op}}\). Here internal map weights are summed, while Hom within each weight retains its required products. A finite-quotient bar model uses shifted operator order, bounds zero-mode bar length at each cutoff, and has polynomial zero-mode outputs. An independently defined diagonal map gives the compatible square. A filtered chain contraction supplies a strictly unital augmented \(A_\infty\) quasi-inverse and a homotopy of the dual square. Ordinary composition has complementary level \(-\ell-\operatorname{Kill}_{\mathfrak g}\). The theorem includes degenerate forms, raw level zero, and the critical form. The full regular contragredient, same-level ordinary-composition and native collision comparisons remain separate.

statements.title: The ambient contragredient vacuum and a finite-energy obstruction
statements.text: With the same affine data, take the full algebraic dual separately in each energy component of a graded-projective vacuum resolution. Its direct sum over energies is a graded-injective resolution of the contragredient vacuum. Signed transposition gives \(\operatorname{rev}_E A_s\simeq R\operatorname{End}^{\mathrm{wt}}_{U_\ell}(D V_\ell)\) in ordinary composition order, where \(\operatorname{rev}_E\) reverses internal map weights. The transpose subalgebra consists of maps continuous for the degreewise weak topology. For nonzero semisimple \(\mathfrak g\), the natural inclusion of lower-bounded modules with finite-dimensional energy spaces into all graded modules misses the horizontal \(H^3(\mathfrak g;\mathbb C)\) self-extension classes. Thus this inclusion is not derived fully faithful. The full regular module has infinite-dimensional energy-zero space and requires a different comparison.

statements.title: Intrinsic vacuum marks and the modular BRST correction
statements.text: For every finite-dimensional complex Lie algebra, retain smoothness and joint nilpotence of the positive-current action. Under the specified generic line-action inputs, the intrinsic category has the bounded-below equivalence and smooth full-faithfulness comparison, including the actual vacuum and augmentation marks, homogeneous endomorphisms and heart kernel. Intermediate energy spaces may be infinite-dimensional. With \(\delta(x)=\operatorname{tr}(\operatorname{ad}x)\), the differential \(Q_\delta=Q+c_0(\delta)\) gives the corrected semiregular coreflector for ordinary smooth modules and bounded-below direct-sum complexes. The unmodified functor carries the negative-character twist. The diagonal comparison is the enhanced counit/augmentation comparison on the intrinsic image. Arbitrary unbounded totals, coefficientwise BRST-to-diagonal maps, the full regular contragredient and native collision comparisons remain separate.

rows.name: Affine algebras at rational level
rows.summary: Noncritical universal affine collision products are identified with vertex tensor products using the required resonance lattices. Positive-integral derived products retain an additional loop-space factor. Broader simple-quotient duality and physical or quantum-group comparisons remain separate from these universal-category results.

statements.title: Noncritical rational fusion and resonance
statements.text: Let \(\mathfrak g\) be a finite-dimensional simple complex Lie algebra with long-root square two, \(k\in\mathbb Q\), and \(\kappa=k+h^\vee\ne0\). On finitely generated smooth universal-affine modules locally finite under \(\mathfrak g[[z]]\), with their Sugawara grading-restricted generalized module structure, the rational-current fusion product represents the Huang–Lepowsky–Zhang \(P(z)\)-intertwining maps for \(z\ne0\). For finite-dimensional Weyl tops, its associator and braiding are obtained by reducing the KZ operators on formal fusion lattices over \(\mathbb C[[\varepsilon]]\) at \(\kappa+\varepsilon\); direct evaluation is valid when constituent conformal weights have no nonzero integral differences in each pairwise and triple top tensor product. Resonant lattices can be nonstandard, so an unqualified substitution into a generic KZ matrix is insufficient.

statements.title: The loop-space factor in positive-integral derived fusion
Curved duals of simple rational quotients
statements.text: For a finite-dimensional simple complex \(\mathfrak g\) and a simple admissible or negative-rational affine quotient \(L_k(\mathfrak g)\) over \(\mathbb C\), construct a complete curved dual incorporating the full null-field ideal and prove an equivalence with an explicitly defined category of discrete smooth \(L_k(\mathfrak g)\)-modules. The comparison must retain the simple vacuum and its collision products; the universal Tate-Lie cochain dual alone does not impose those null relations.

statements.title: The root-of-unity fibre comparison
statements.text: For the represented affine collision product at positive integral level over \(\mathbb C\), compare the long bimodule fibre over \(\mathbb C^I\), where \(I\) indexes integrable simple modules, and its weak Hopf reconstruction with a precisely specified root-of-unity quantum-group category or its semisimplification. The comparison must identify the parameter, associator, braiding and quotient maps. Admissible and negative-rational simple quotients require separate choices of category and recipient; an ordinary strong monoidal fibre to vector spaces is not assumed.

rows.name: Affine algebras at critical level
rows.summary: The universal critical algebra remains curved on the dual side, and its smooth vacuum self-extensions contain differential forms on opers. Algebraic induction remains an equivalence after its exact detected localization. Under the coherent native-action, tensor–\(\operatorname{Hom}\) and common-lower-energy actual-unit/full-faithfulness hypotheses, a nonzero ordinary critical telescope has zero smooth realization, so the ordinary global unit fails. Presentable categorical self-duality survives, but the compact category has no right Serre functor; collision fusion and lines over opers remain open.

statements.title: Criticality does not remove curvature
statements.text: Over \(\mathbb C\), let \(\mathfrak g\ne0\) be finite-dimensional and simple, with invariant form \(B\) normalized by long-root square two, and take its universal untwisted affine algebra at \(k=-h^\vee\), without a degree derivation. Its curved point dual is \((C^\bullet_{\mathrm{cont}}(\mathfrak g((z))),d_{\mathrm{CE}},\eta_{-h^\vee})\), where \(\eta_k(xz^m,yz^n)=kmB(x,y)\delta_{m+n,0}\); completion is separately by finite negative-mode subsets in each exterior degree, with finite positive support for each subset and no product over exterior degrees. For \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\), normalized by \(B(h,h)=2\), the commuting pair \(hz,hz^{-1}\) has curvature \(-4\), so this cocycle is not exact. The vanishing shifted level \(k+h^\vee=0\) therefore supplies no uncurving of this model.

statements.title: Self-duality without a compact Serre functor
statements.text: For a nonzero finite-dimensional simple complex \(\mathfrak g\), use discrete smooth modules of its untwisted affine algebra at \(k=-h^\vee\), without a degree derivation. Let \(\mathcal C\) be the idempotent-complete thick dg subcategory of the ordinary derived category generated by algebraic inductions from finite-dimensional smooth representations of central inverse images of compact open Lie subalgebras, and let \(\mathcal S=\operatorname{Ind}(\mathcal C)\). There is no functor \(S:\mathcal C\to\mathcal C\) with natural complex-linear isomorphisms \(\operatorname{Hom}(A,B)^*\cong\operatorname{Hom}(B,SA)\), where Hom means degree-zero derived Hom and the star is the full algebraic dual. Nevertheless \(\mathcal S^\vee\simeq\mathcal S\) as presentable dg categories under the semi-infinite pairing.

statements.title: Critical vacuum self-extensions
statements.text: For a finite-dimensional simple complex \(\mathfrak g\), normalized by long-root square two, let \(V^{-h^\vee}\) be the universal affine vacuum in the category of discrete smooth fixed-level modules. Writing \(Z=\mathcal O(\operatorname{Op}_{{}^LG}(\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb C[[z]]))\) for its regular-disc oper centre, one has \(\operatorname{Ext}^\bullet(V^{-h^\vee},V^{-h^\vee})\cong\Omega_Z^\bullet\otimes H^\bullet(\mathfrak g;\mathbb C)\); the constant-\(\mathfrak g\)-relative version omits the last factor. The differential from first-order variation of the level acts as \(d_{\mathrm{dR}}\otimes1\).
statements.cite: Edward Frenkel and Constantin Teleman, Self-extensions of Verma modules and differential forms on opers (2006), Theorem 4.4 and Proposition 4.6.

statements.title: Critical collision over opers
statements.text: For a finite-dimensional simple complex \(\mathfrak g\) and universal affine modules at \(k=-h^\vee\), construct collision fusion and a category of lines over the regular-disc oper centre, with coherent associativity, units and the compatible action of the critical central currents. The construction must recover separated-point Gaudin operators without dividing by \(k+h^\vee\), and specify how it behaves under specialization of the oper.

statements.title: The critical translation cone retains kernel and cokernel data
statements.text:
For the two-term translation object \(z_{\rm top}=\operatorname{fib}(T:Z\to Z)\), its cohomology fits into \(0\to\operatorname{coker}(T:H^{n-1}Z\to H^{n-1}Z)\to H^n(z_{\rm top})\to\ker(T:H^nZ\to H^nZ)\to0\). At critical level it cannot simply be identified with the oper-form cohomology of the input \(Z\).

Scope: This is the formal consequence of the stated translation-cone definition. It does not identify an actual universal critical action space, construct its \(E_2\) structure, or transfer a bracket.

rows.name: Virasoro algebras, finite categories and continuous series
rows.summary: Universal curved duality, supported induction, finite-sector Ward products and minimal-model reconstruction are established. Under the normalized boundary hypothesis \(H\), analytic estimates and positive-label pentagon, every fixed finite positive word has completed sewing and coherent tree comparisons. One vacuum input, retained original spectra and a three-input vacuum output have their precise source and output domains. The intrinsic input category for arbitrary recipient objects, generic partner Hilbert comparison and independent state preparation remain separate.

statements.title: The universal curved Virasoro dual
statements.text: For the universal Virasoro algebra over \(\mathbb C\) at any \(c\in\mathbb C\), use \(\mathfrak w=\mathbb C((z))\partial_z\), positive polarization \(P=\prod_{n\ge-1}\mathbb CL_n\), and negative modes \(D=\bigoplus_{n\le-2}\mathbb CL_n\). Its point dual is the curved continuous Chevalley–Eilenberg algebra \((B_c,d,\Omega_c)\), where \(d\alpha(x,y)=-\alpha([x,y])\) and \(\Omega_c(L_m,L_n)=c(m^3-m)\delta_{m+n,0}/12\). In degree \(q\), \(B_c\) is a product over finite negative-mode subsets of size at most \(q\), with finite positive-dual support separately in every factor; there is no product over exterior degrees. This computation is for the universal envelope and does not supply the curved dual of a simple quotient.

statements.title: A charge-independent universal vacuum model
statements.text: Over \(\mathbb C\), for every complex \(c\), let \(\mathrm{Vir}_c\) be the universal vacuum and \(W_1=\prod_{m\ge-1}\mathbb CL_m\) the formal regular-vector-field algebra. On continuous finite-jet cochains, the inclusion \(C^\bullet_{\mathrm{cont}}(W_1;\mathbb C)\hookrightarrow C^\bullet_{\mathrm{cont}}(W_1;\mathrm{Vir}_c)\) is a central, commutative dg vertex quasi-isomorphism. Universal vacuum self-Ext in discrete smooth modules is \(\Lambda(\omega_3)\), \(|\omega_3|=3\), and this supplies a strictly unital commutative \(E_3\)-model whose Browder bracket vanishes. Identifying this model with geometric mixed bulk/boundary operations is a separate open comparison.

statements.title: Minimal models and a finite weak Hopf algebra
statements.text: For coprime integers \(2\le p<q\), put \(c_{p,q}=1-6(p-q)^2/(pq)\), and take finite direct sums of ordinary simple modules of the simple Virasoro vertex algebra \(L(c_{p,q},0)\) over \(\mathbb C\). The output constructed from full rational Ward invariants at distinct points agrees with the vertex \(P(z)\)-tensor product, with common continuation paths and the simple vacuum as unit. If \(I\) indexes the simple modules, the exact faithful long bimodule fibre \(F(M)=\bigoplus_{i,j\in I}\operatorname{Hom}(L_i,M\boxtimes L_j)\) takes values in \(\mathbb C^I\)-bimodules and reconstructs a finite weak Hopf algebra whose finite module category has the same ribbon structure. Its tensor unit projector is \(\Delta(1)\), and its scalar counit need not be a character; this statement concerns the finite simple-quotient category, not all modules of rational central charge.

statements.title: The degenerate field algebra generated by two doublets
statements.text: Over \(\mathbb C\), fix \(b\ne0\), \(t=b^2\notin\mathbb Q\), and \(c=13+6(t+t^{-1})\). Let \(\mathcal C\) be the finite-length, lower-bounded, \(C_1\)-cofinite Virasoro vertex tensor category, with simple modules \(L_{r,s}\), \(r,s\ge1\), of weights \(((t+1)^2-(rt+s)^2)/(4t)\), and fix its parity-corrected two-row quantum-group fibre \(\omega\) and coherent tensorator. The algebraic sum \[A_\omega=\bigoplus_{r,s\ge1}L_{r,s}\otimes\omega(L_{r,s})^*\quad\text{in }\operatorname{Ind}(\mathcal C)\] has unital, translation-covariant associative intertwining fields on universal covers of ordered configuration spaces. Each finite input has finitely many output sectors; only the weights within each sector are completed, with restricted output duals and finite-dimensional sums below every real-part weight bound. The known finite-input vertex-tensor convergence theorem applies on chosen branches, including nonreal \(t\). The right action of \(U_{e^{-\pi it}}(\mathfrak{sl}_2)\otimes U_{e^{-\pi i/t}}(\mathfrak{sl}_2)\) on multiplicity duals preserves the fields, and its invariant fields are exactly the Virasoro vacuum algebra. Over that algebra, the highest-state doublets of \(L_{2,1}\) and \(L_{1,2}\), their descendants and iterated field coefficients generate every multiplicity space. Exchange is the constant dual inverse of the parity-corrected fibre braid; the mixed fundamental full turn is the known value \(-1\). The fields have noninteger powers; for positive real irrational \(t\), the algebraic sector sum is not globally lower-bounded.
statements.antecedents: Creutzig et al. (2020, preprint), Theorem 3.1.4, Proposition 4.2.4 and Theorems 5.2.2, 5.2.5; Huang–Lepowsky–Zhang VII (2011, preprint), Theorem 11.8(2); Koshida (2022, preprint), Theorems 5.7, 5.10, 5.11; Etingof–Gelaki–Nikshych–Ostrik (2015), Theorem 5.4.1 and Examples 7.9.10–11; Huang–Kong (2003, preprint), Proposition 2.7 and Theorem 4.3; Cremmer–Gervais–Roussel (1993), §§3, 5, especially equations (5.7)–(5.12).

statements.title: Singular sewing requires full radical descent
statements.text: Over \(\mathbb C\), take \(b\ne0\), \(b^2\notin\mathbb Q\), \(c=1+6(b+b^{-1})^2\), and \(h_{r,s}=((b+b^{-1})^2-(rb+s/b)^2)/4\), with \(r,s\ge1\). For fixed external weights and two coefficient-one three-point Ward forms, if both forms annihilate the entire radical of \(M(c,h_{r,s})\), the Verma block limit as the intermediate weight tends to \(h_{r,s}\) exists coefficient by coefficient and equals sewing through the simple quotient. At each descendant level every positive Smith exponent of the Gram family is one; this is the transversality that makes the conclusion follow from descent. At \(c=1\), intermediate weight \(1/4\) and four fixed external weights \(1/16\), both forms descend at every level but the level-two Verma limit exceeds the quotient coefficient by \(1/768\), so the irrational theorem cannot be specialized without an additional condition.

statements.title: Formal Beltrami sources and Ward insertions
statements.text: For the universal Virasoro vacuum over \(\mathbb C\) at any \(c\), let \(\mu\) be a formal series with zero constant term in finitely many commuting parameters, with smooth compactly supported coefficients on a planar sphere chart. With \(\bar\partial(z-w)^{-1}=\pi\delta^2(z-w)\), source coupling \(-\pi^{-1}\int\mu T\,d^2z\), and \(f_\mu\) normalized by \(\bar\partial f_\mu=\mu f_\mu'\), \(f_\mu=z+O(z^{-1})\), the normalized vacuum functional \(Z_c=e^{W_c}\) satisfies \(-\pi\delta W_c/\delta\mu=(c/12)\operatorname{Sch}(f_\mu)\) and \(W_c[0]=0\). Nested annular mode insertions with zero/one cutoff plateaux recover the ordered vacuum matrix coefficients, and the punctured-flow identity determines the contact terms for overlapping cutoffs; other plateau values require weighted residues. These are identities of continuous formal source coefficients, with no assertion of convergence in \(\mu\).

statements.title: Continuous fusion with arbitrary recipient inputs
statements.text: For real \(c>1\), construct an intrinsic admissible source assignment for arbitrary objects of the common continuous Ward recipient, and prove the corresponding represented fusion category with compatible repeated collisions and inverse domains. Fixed positive point-module inputs already have a representing recipient; full five-point interior sewing, entangled mixed Ward identities and coefficient-one vacuum units hold on their declared stages under \(H\) and the retained analytic hypotheses. The actual outer primary sewing does not extend to the whole common recipient, so its finer cluster-quotient source must be retained in the categorical construction. Preserve the separate geometric tree theorem at fixed \(c>25\).

statements.title: Completed principal sewing and the geometric tree sector
statements.text: For every real \(c>1\), compact-uniform three-leg estimates give exponentially weighted input maps, a nonempty two-successive-insertion domain with strict radius loss, and a local five-principal sewing germ. Internal momentum tails remain uncut. The stated four-point boundary-input hypothesis is retained where used. At each fixed \(c>25\), a separate geometric theorem supplies finite-tree local sewing and principal-marked sphere-tree Hilbert/channel comparison on Teichmüller space. It retains the Schwarzian and decoration lines and internal-momentum-dependent phases. The later fixed-positive-input theorem gives a common recipient representing the declared continuous rational Ward operations, and full five-point interior sewing holds under its stated \(H\) and analytic hypotheses. An intrinsic source category for arbitrary recipient objects, stable under the required repeated collisions, remains open.

statements.title: Five-point collar coherence with four completed inputs
statements.text: For real \(c>1\), positive principal momenta and the stated positive Shapovalov and four-point boundary-input hypothesis \(H\), five independently constructed sewing maps extend to all four completed inputs on one entire-energy Fréchet domain. They take values in a fixed regularized output space over the five collar strips. A finite input exponent may depend on a compact position set; the sufficient collar widths remain non-effective. The five flip identities hold on their overlaps, and the independent spectral-label pentagon gives collar coherence. The corresponding typed positive spectral category has natural bounded spectral morphisms and closed unitary associators, with inverses on the same output energy scales. Its mode domain has compact total-output spectrum and finite output level; intermediate spectra need not be compact. Full integer-mode Ward covariance includes the normally convergent negative-mode sum on strengthened inputs. External spectral measures remain multiplicities, and fusion retains its canonical output measure. The generating function has radius at least one; the stated removable singularity at \(c=25\) still refutes universal exact radius one. Separate results now give full five-point interior sewing under \(H\) and the retained analytic hypotheses, point and meromorphic target recipients, full mixed rational Ward identities and coefficient-one units for every placement of one vacuum. Fixed positive point-module inputs have a common representing recipient for the declared operations. The remaining categorical question is an intrinsic source assignment for arbitrary recipient objects and repeated collisions; higher-arity interior sewing keeps its additional domain requirements.

statements.title: Four-point comparison on completed descendant inputs
statements.text: For real central charge in a compact subset of \((1,\infty)\) and positive principal momenta, all-descendant middle-leg doubling gives a common completed four-point comparison under the stated boundary-input hypothesis. All three finite input legs lie in weighted Hilbert spaces with exponent \(t>T_K\), depending on the position compact. The spectator/output exponent remains \(s>\max(A_0/2,\log L/2)\). The construction is bounded in the prescribed direct-integral Hilbert and Bochner \(L^1\) targets and retains the actual channel branches. Its atomless decomposable operator is not globally Hilbert–Schmidt. A separate five-point theorem now admits four entire-energy inputs across the full ordered interior under \(H\) and the retained analytic hypotheses. Mixed completed vacuum sewings have their coefficient-one unit triangles, and fixed positive inputs have a representing Ward recipient. Arbitrary recipient sources, repeated collisions and all-arity interior sewing retain their further requirements.

statements.title: Conditional extremal and Parseval comparisons
statements.text: For \(k>1\) and \(0<t<1\), let \(w\) be a positive continuous translation-periodic weight on the upper half-plane with \(0<a\le w(\tau)y^{2-k}\operatorname{ht}(\tau)^{k-3/2}\le A<\infty\), where \(y=\operatorname{Im}\tau\) and \(\operatorname{ht}\) is modular height. Its \(t\)-quasiperiodic holomorphic fibre has an extremal orthogonal basis. Complete block reciprocity is equivalent to identifying the blocks with that basis and their prescribed norms. Under a faithful holomorphic block realization with bounded evaluations, an absolutely convergent monomial Gram identity gives isometric comparison of the polynomial closures. Density in the coefficient space and density in the full Bergman space are distinct requirements. A one-sided kernel inequality yields equality when the exact total traces agree. Global modular dimension formulas additionally require full covariance and the fixed cocycle. These criteria do not prove the physical nonlinear Gram identity, either density condition, positivity or cusp control; numerical trace agreement does not discharge an exact identity.

statements.title: Completed vacuum placements and the resolved nested norm
statements.text: Under the same real \(c>1\) analytic and boundary-input hypotheses, a rapid completed vacuum module \(V_\nu\) acts on finite exponential principal-input stages on the stated strict annuli. Its two placements are \(Y(\omega,z)\) and \(e^{zL_{-1}}Y(\omega,-z)\), with the prescribed translation margins; the vacuum vector has coefficient one. Actual Ward compatibility extends to completed inputs with all principal spectra retained. Separately, for fixed positive external labels the resolved three-input vector retains its intermediate multiplicity label and satisfies \(\|V\|^2=2^{-1/2}N\); the vector \(2^{1/4}V\) has norm squared \(N\). The proof sums the outer vacuum series after the finite Ward operations and then continues the resulting holomorphic pairing. It does not flatten both raw vacuum series into one unrestricted absolute double series or compute the norm after integrating out multiplicity. Coefficient-one unit triangles now hold for all four mixed vacuum placements on their specified rapid or strengthened endpoint stages. This does not replace the rapid vacuum source by an arbitrary exponential source or make every common-recipient output an input to another sewing.

statements.title: The reflected Virasoro category and its actual marks
statements.text: For every complex charge \(c\), the specified line dg algebra \(Y_c\) acts coherently on the resolution and weight-pro carrier of \(W_{26-c}\). The actual right-action map preserves differential and opposite composition. It gives the declared cohomologically bounded-below enhanced equivalence, including the full subcategory of bounded-below smooth Virasoro complexes of charge \(26-c\) whose cohomology is jointly nilpotent under the positive subalgebra \(\mathfrak n_2\); no lower internal-energy bound is imposed. The inverse, unit and counit are explicit. The regular module maps to \(W\), the universal-vacuum mark to \(V_{26-c}\), and the augmentation to the restricted contragredient \(D_\sigma V_{26-c}\). The internal weight completion and derived bimodule comparison are essential; this is not a strict full action on the degree-zero module alone. The full unbounded reflected null class is now classified by the line charge: ordinary acyclics occur away from the stated coprime minimal-series values, and actual acyclic telescopes retain reflected classes at those values. Native supported induction has a separately computed kernel and continuous separated tensorator. The relation between its weak class and ordinary equivalences, the remaining collision comparisons and physical realization retain their own targets.

statements.title: Augmentation Ext at nonsimple reflected charges
statements.text: For every complex \(c\), the ordinary derived endomorphism algebra of the reflected augmentation is formal and quasi-isomorphic to \(\Lambda(\eta_3)\), with \(|\eta_3|=3\). For the normalized map \(q:V_{26-c}\to D_\sigma V_{26-c}\), both actual maps \[R\operatorname{End}(V)\longrightarrow R\operatorname{Hom}(V,D_\sigma V)\longleftarrow R\operatorname{End}(D_\sigma V)\] are quasi-isomorphisms. A homotopy-commuting-square construction turns them into a unital dg-algebra roof in ordinary composition order. At nonsimple charges, \(q\) remains noninvertible and its cone is nonzero, even though \(R\operatorname{Hom}(V,\operatorname{Cone}q)=0\) and \(R\operatorname{Hom}(\operatorname{Cone}q,D_\sigma V)=0\). These two vanishing tests do not establish conservativity or identify the full unbounded null class. The universal vacuum, its contragredient and its simple quotient remain distinct.

statements.title: A bare exterior E3 algebra has no coupling parameter
statements.text:
A strictly unital \(E_3\)-algebra over \(\mathbb C\) with cohomology \(\Lambda(x_3)\), \(|x_3|=3\), is unique up to equivalence at the level of its bare \(E_3\) structure. That structure alone therefore supplies no varying coupling scalar. A filtration, mixed action, retained translation or central-charge class, marked comparison, or braided category is additional data.

Scope: This is single-generator exterior rigidity. It is not a rigidity theorem for arbitrary simple affine cohomology, and uniqueness does not construct an enhancement on a separately prescribed object. Rank-one coefficient Koszul comparisons retain their specified unipotent sector and separate charge grading; no full all-charge braided equivalence follows from bare formality.
hypotheses: This is single-generator exterior rigidity. It is not a rigidity theorem for arbitrary simple affine cohomology, and uniqueness does not construct an enhancement on a separately prescribed object.
Rank-one coefficient Koszul comparisons retain their specified unipotent sector and separate charge grading; no full all-charge braided equivalence follows from bare formality.

rows.name: \(W\)-algebras and quantum Drinfeld–Sokolov reduction
rows.summary: Universal \(W\)-algebras have finite vacuum-extension models, generic exterior answers and explicit exceptional \(W_4\) cohomology. A curved bar construction recognizes all weak regular \(W_3\) modules, and the stated irrational sector cohomology is known. The localized nonlinear derived equivalence, exceptional products, reduction-compatible physical action and higher-rank states remain work.

statements.title: Finite vacuum models and exterior algebras
statements.text: Let \(\mathfrak g\) be a finite-dimensional simple complex Lie algebra of rank \(r\), with exponents \(m_i\), and let \(V=W^k(\mathfrak g)\) be its universal principal \(W\)-algebra, retaining the universal generators at special levels. In the category \(\mathcal S_k\) of all weak modules, at every noncritical level \(k\ne-h^\vee\), absolute \(\operatorname{Ext}^{\bullet}_{\mathcal S_k}(V,V)\) is computed by a bounded finite-dimensional conformal-weight-zero complex and has Euler characteristic zero. Outside a finite rational set of noncritical levels, it is \(\Lambda_{\mathbb C}(\eta_1,\ldots,\eta_r)\), with \(|\eta_i|=2m_i+1\), and the associative derived endomorphism algebra is \(A_\infty\)-formal, in particular for every \(k\notin\mathbb Q\). For \(\mathfrak{sl}_3\) and \(\mathfrak{so}_5\), the exterior answer and formality hold at every noncritical level, respectively as \(\Lambda(\eta_3,\eta_5)\) and \(\Lambda(\eta_3,\eta_7)\); the \(\mathfrak{sl}_3\) result includes \(k=-12/5,-4/3\), where \(c=-22/5\).
statements.antecedents: De Sole–Kac (2005); Bakalov–Kac–Voronov (1999); Raskin (2016); Dhillon (2019); Bouwknegt–McCarthy–Pilch (1996); Zhu (1994).

statements.title: Exceptional universal \(W_4\) self-extensions
statements.text: Over \(\mathbb C\), let \(V=W^k(\mathfrak{sl}_4)\) be universal, with \(\tau=k+4\in\{3/2,-3/2,2/3,-2/3\}\), and take absolute Ext in all weak modules. Its Poincaré polynomial is \(1+t^3+t^5+t^7+2t^8+t^9+t^{10}+t^{11}+2t^{12}+t^{15}\), so its total dimension is twelve. Nonzero generators of the degree-three, degree-five and degree-seven spaces satisfy \(\eta_3\eta_5\ne0\), \(\eta_3\eta_7\ne0\) and \(\eta_5\eta_7=0\); at \(\tau=\pm3/2\), the canonical Drinfeld–Sokolov map \(\Lambda(\theta_3,\theta_5,\theta_7)\to\operatorname{Ext}^{\bullet}(V,V)\) has kernel \((\theta_5\theta_7)\). Multiplication involving the additional classes and associative formality at these levels remain open.
statements.antecedents: Raskin (2016); Dhillon (2019); Drinfeld–Gaitsgory (2011); Boonstra (1994); De Sole–Kac (2005); Braverman–Gaitsgory (1996).

statements.title: A curved bar construction for all weak \(W_3\)-modules
statements.text: For every \(c\in\mathbb C\), let \(V_c\) be the regular universal \(W_3\)-algebra, let \(A_c\) be the closure of its finite mode operations for pointwise convergence on discrete cyclic weak modules, and set \(e(a)=\pi_0(a\mathbf1)\), \(E=\ker e\), where \(\pi_0\) projects onto the vacuum-weight line. The curved bar algebra \(\widehat B=\prod_{n\ge0}\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb C}(E^{\otimes n},\mathbb C)\), with algebraic tensors, the topology annihilating finite-dimensional finite-length tensor spaces, graded-opposite bar multiplication and curvature \(h(a,b)=e(ab)\), has free contramodules \(B[[M]]^r=\prod_{n\ge0}\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb C}(E^{\otimes n},M^{r-n})\); twisting gives a dg adjunction \(K\dashv F\) for possibly unbounded smooth complexes, with \(F(Q)^r=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{cont}}(A_c,Q^r_{\mathrm{disc}})\). Curved contramodules free on degree-zero generators \(M\), with every recovered orbit map \(a\mapsto e(a)m+(Dm)(a-e(a)1)\) continuous into discrete \(M\), form an abelian category exactly equivalent to all weak \(V_c\)-modules. For ordinary weak modules, bar cochains continuous successively in the mode inputs, with each intermediate Hom space treated as discrete, compute derived Hom and Yoneda composition.
statements.antecedents: Beilinson (2007); De Sole–Kac (2005); Al-Ali–Linshaw (2016); Positselski (2009); Clarke–Crossley–Whitehouse (2006); Bousfield (2003); Damiolini–Gibney–Tarasca (2019).

statements.title: Braided quantum Hamiltonian reduction
statements.text: Let \(\mathfrak g\) be a simple complex Lie algebra of type \(A,D\) or \(E\), let \(k\in\mathbb C\setminus\mathbb Q\), and let \(f\in\mathfrak g\) be any nilpotent element. Quantum Hamiltonian reduction \(H_f^0\) is a braided tensor equivalence between the category of finite direct sums of affine Weyl modules \(\mathbb V^k_\lambda\), induced from finite-dimensional simple \(\mathfrak g\)-modules of dominant integral highest weight \(\lambda\), and the category of finite direct sums of their reductions as \(W^k(\mathfrak g,f)\)-modules. The reduced category is rigid, with \(H_f^0(\mathbb V^k_{\lambda^*})\) dual to \(H_f^0(\mathbb V^k_\lambda)\), where \(\lambda^*\) labels the dual finite-dimensional representation.
statements.cite: Creutzig–Dhillon–Nakatsuka, [The Kazhdan–Lusztig category of W-algebras of simply-laced Lie algebras at irrational levels](https://arxiv.org/html/2603.04667) (2026), Theorems 1.1 and 5.2; §§2.1–2.2.

statements.title: Nonlinear derived duality and exceptional products
statements.text: For universal principal \(W_3\) and \(W_4\) over \(\mathbb C\), construct a polarized completed curved dual, define the null classes on smooth complexes and contramodules, and prove that the twisting adjunction induces an equivalence after localization. The comparison must preserve the vacuum and intertwine quantum Drinfeld–Sokolov reduction; its extension to rational simple quotients remains a separate question. For \(W^k(\mathfrak{sl}_4)\) with \(k+4=\pm3/2,\pm2/3\), determine the remaining products, associative formality and the orders of the two local torsion summands.

statements.title: Irrational W₃ sector cohomology
statements.text: For \(K\in\mathbb C\setminus\mathbb Q\) and dominant integral \(\mathfrak{sl}_3\) weights \(\lambda,\mu,\lambda^{\prime},\mu^{\prime}\), use the explicit paired \(W_3\) BRST complex \(T_{\lambda,\mu}(K)\otimes T_{\lambda^{\prime},\mu^{\prime}}(-K)\), with \(c(K)=50-24K-24/K\) and \(c(-K)=100-c(K)\). Its cohomology vanishes unless \((\lambda^{\prime},\mu^{\prime})=(\lambda^*,\mu)\). On the partner, its cohomology is one-dimensional in each of degrees \(0,3,5,8\) and zero otherwise. The proof uses the nonzero primitive-cover transgression from the Jantzen connecting map and the unique on-shell coresolution column; the bottom differential is its transferred projection. This is a graded-vector-space theorem. It does not construct sector multiplication, a two-row vertex algebra, a braid-reversed equivalence, arbitrary-module derived \(\operatorname{Hom}\) or a rational-level extension.

rows.name: Yangians, the Yang double and rational quantum vertex algebras
rows.summary: The restricted RTT ghost vacuum has its exchange, graded vacuum cohomology and monoidal Koszul cochains on bounded-below finite-type lattices. Full smooth derived duality requires compatible finite-precision constructions and explicit weak classes. Fixed-level boundary collision must also be compared with the level-additive spectral coproduct.

statements.title: The RTT ghost dual vacuum
statements.text: For the crossing-normalized RTT double of \(\mathfrak{gl}_n\) over \(\mathbb C\), \(n\ge2\), with arbitrary central level \(K\), formal \(\hbar\) of weight \(-1\) and no determinant-one quotient, use torsion-free weight-graded lattices complete separately in each weight, with finite-dimensional classical weight spaces vanishing below weight zero, and take the \(\hbar\)-adic completion for vertex operations. Its dual vacuum has odd generators \(c_{ij,s}\) of cohomological degree one and weight \(s-1\), with \(c(y)=\sum_{s\ge1}c_sy^{s-1}\), \(dc(y)=-c(y)^2\), \(Tc_s=sc_{s+1}\), and \[c_{ij}(y)c_{kl}(y')+c_{kl}(y')c_{ij}(y)=\frac{\hbar}{y-y'}\bigl(c_{kj}(y)-c_{kj}(y')\bigr)\bigl(c_{il}(y)-c_{il}(y')\bigr).\] Ordered exterior monomials give a topological basis, and the fields \(Y(a,z)b=(e^{zT}a)b\) have a unique unitary, translation-covariant exchange compatible with the differential, the Yang–Baxter equation and both hexagons. Its coefficient of \(\hbar^j\) on homogeneous inputs \(a,b\) has pole order at most \(j+\operatorname{wt}(a)+\operatorname{wt}(b)\).
statements.antecedents: Gui–Li–Zeng (2022); Li (2008); Gurevich (1990); Wambst (1993); Etingof–Kazhdan (2000); Jing–Kožić–Molev–Yang (2016).

statements.title: Monoidal Koszul cochains and spectral fusion
statements.text: Over \(\mathbb C\), for the normalized \(\mathfrak{gl}_n\) Yangian with \(n\ge2\), formal \(\hbar\) of weight \(-1\) and no determinant-one quotient, let \(M,N\) be torsion-free weightwise complete lattices whose classical weight spaces are finite-dimensional and vanish below weight zero. If \(B\) is the RTT ghost dual vacuum and \(K(M)\) denotes restricted graded Koszul cochains with coefficients in \(M\), the dressed left \(B\)-action and the coaction cup product give \(K(M)\widehat\otimes_BK(N)\simeq K(M\widehat\otimes N)\). With \(\sigma_zT^*(u)=T^*(u-z)\), the coproduct \(\Delta_z=(\sigma_z\otimes1)\Delta\) satisfies \((\Delta_x\otimes1)\Delta_y=(1\otimes\Delta_y)\Delta_{x+y}\) on the rational representatives before their Laurent expansions at separated spectral points. The central coproduct adds boundary levels, and the fundamental intertwiner \(1-\hbar P/(y-y')\) becomes invertible after spectral localization; at numerical \(\hbar\), this requires \(y-y'\ne0\) and \((y-y')^2\ne\hbar^2\).

statements.title: Noncritical graded vacuum cohomology
statements.text: Let \(V_K\) be the universal normalized RTT vacuum of \(\mathfrak{gl}_n\) over \(\mathbb C\), \(n\ge2\), with \(K\ne-n\), formal \(\hbar\) of weight \(-1\), no determinant-one quotient and scalar affine form \(\kappa_K(X,Y)=K(\operatorname{tr}(XY)-\operatorname{tr}(X)\operatorname{tr}(Y)/n)\). In the category of torsion-free weightwise complete graded lattices bounded below and of finite type, the one-vacuum Koszul complex is a dg \(\hbar\)-adic quantum vertex superalgebra whose cohomology is torsion-free and has topological basis \[\mathbb C[d_r:r\ge0]\otimes\Lambda(\lambda_s:s\ge2)\otimes H^*(\mathfrak{gl}_n;\mathbb C).\] Here \(\sum_{r\ge0}d_rv^r=(1-\operatorname{qdet}T(v))/\hbar\), \(\lambda_s=\operatorname{tr}c_s\), and \(H^*(\mathfrak{gl}_n)=\Lambda(\eta_1,\eta_3,\ldots,\eta_{2n-1})\), with \(\eta_1=\lambda_1\). The cohomology fields are regular and supercommutative, with \(Td_r=(r+1)d_{r+1}\) and \(T\lambda_s=s\lambda_{s+1}\).

statements.title: Smooth quantum duality
statements.text: For the normalized \(\mathfrak{gl}_n\) Yang double, \(n\ge2\), over \(\mathbb C[\hbar]/(\hbar^N)\), construct twisting and coinduction functors between smooth modules and curved contramodules that satisfy the curvature, Leibniz and adjunction identities, and prove an equivalence in explicitly defined derived localizations. Establish compatibility as \(N\) varies before passing to a formal limit. Separately, construct fixed-level boundary collision products and compare them with the level-additive central coproduct.

rows.name: Trigonometric and elliptic spectral parameters
rows.summary: Scalar multiplicative theories and all-order elliptic quantum vertex fields are constructed on their declared formal carriers. The scalar-corrected, ordered \(\mathcal H_5\) realization has full native \(Y_{\le5},S_{\le6}\), all-order moments and formal global descent. The zero-sixth-pair target has no admitted next-order extension; the distinct \(Y_6^\ddagger\) target has all-order fields. Its moment/global applications, full enlarged-category recognition and analytic or physical sewing remain separate.

statements.title: Scalar trigonometric fields
statements.text: Put \(P=\mathbb C[x_0,x_1,\ldots]\), \(Tx_r=x_{r+1}\), and \(V=P[[\hbar]]\), completed only in \(\hbar\). The Wick extension of the contraction \(\hbar/(e^u-1)\), with \(J=x_0\) and \(Y(J,u)J=(e^{uT}J)J+\hbar/(e^u-1)\), gives a quantum vertex algebra with field target \(P((u))[[\hbar]]\) and exchange target \((P\otimes P\otimes\mathbb C[q,q^{-1},(q-1)^{-1}])[[\hbar]]\), where \(q=e^u\). Locality is uniform in the spectator at each finite \(\hbar\)-precision, and the exchange satisfies unitarity, Yang–Baxter and both hexagons. There is no uniform pole bound for complete inputs: the exchange of \(\sum_{r\ge0}\hbar^rx_r\) with \(J\) has poles of unbounded order.

statements.title: A completion obstruction to an algebraic polar target
statements.text: Let \(k\) have characteristic zero, \(R=k[[\hbar]]\), let \(V\) be a separated complete flat \(R\)-module, and let \(T\) be an \(R\)-linear endomorphism. If an \(R\)-linear exchange map on \(V\otimes_RV\) takes values in the strictly algebraic target \((V\otimes_RV)\otimes_RR[q,q^{-1},(q-1)^{-1}]\) and satisfies \([T_1,S]=-q\partial_qS\), every output is regular at \(q=1\). A singular exchange on such a complete state module therefore requires a larger target, such as a completion that permits the pole order to grow with \(\hbar\)-precision.

statements.title: Meromorphic Yangian–quantum-loop comparison
statements.text: Let \(\mathfrak g\) be complex semisimple, \(\hbar\notin\mathbb Q\), \(q=e^{\pi i\hbar}\), and \(|q|\ne1\). On finite-dimensional noncongruent Yangian modules, whose poles of each root current \(x_i^\pm(u)\) have no nonzero integral differences, the functor \(\Gamma\) to quantum-loop modules has coherent meromorphic tensorators for the deformed Drinfeld coproducts and preserves the braidings from the commutative parts \(R^0\) of the universal R-matrices. If \(\Pi\subset\mathbb C\) satisfies \((\Pi-\Pi)\cap\mathbb Z=\{0\}\) and \(\Pi\pm\hbar/2\subset\Pi\), then \(\Gamma\) restricts to an equivalence between the finite-dimensional module subcategories whose root-current, Cartan-current and inverse-Cartan-current poles lie respectively in \(\Pi\) and \(\exp(2\pi i\Pi)\), with the meromorphic tensor comparison wherever the shifted products are defined.
statements.cite: Gautam–Toledano Laredo, [Meromorphic tensor equivalence for Yangians and quantum loop algebras](https://arxiv.org/html/1403.5251v6), Publications Mathématiques de l’IHÉS 125 (2017), 267–337, §§2.5–2.6, 6.2–6.5.

statements.title: Elliptic fields with their global coefficients
statements.text: For a complex elliptic curve \(E\), extend scalar bar–cobar duality to matrix-valued meromorphic exchange kernels with a chosen period bundle, and construct compatible state fields and collision operations over \(E\). The construction must specify the allowed polar divisors, the translation action, the period holonomies and the tensor completion, and prove the exchange and associativity identities on those same carriers. Comparing with an elliptic quantum vertex algebra requires identifying its classical state space and its elliptic modulus throughout the deformation.

statements.title: Matrix trigonometric fields in the multiplicative ring
statements.text: In characteristic zero, the homogeneous matrix RTT construction gives integral divided fields, exchange, level-changing coproducts, and cut residues at every finite formal precision. Its spectral values lie in the completed multiplicative ring \(k[x^{\pm1},(x-1)^{-1}]\), with \(x=e^z\). Already at second precision, the displayed form does not belong to the additive Laurent-polynomial ring. A common rational, trigonometric, and monodromic theory must therefore retain the value ring, translation, and positioned tensor maps.

statements.title: Binary Ward data do not determine a charged field family
statements.text: For the translated rational-current module with \(\kappa\lambda\nu\ne0\), one selected inserted primary admits the specified binary construction on every polynomial second input and for every current mode. Its free scalar and shift data can give either an ordinary Laurent example with trivial full turn or the normalized Kummer and Gaussian examples in their larger coefficient algebras. Translation and binary Ward commutators alone therefore do not force the Gaussian monodromy. Fields of arbitrary inserted descendants, vacuum normalization, coherent charge families and ternary collision identities remain separate constraints.

statements.title: Necessary conditions for full RTT recognition
statements.text: In characteristic zero, at nonzero deformation parameter and rank at least two, the fundamental tensor square in the specified full RTT category is absolutely simple and has only scalar endomorphisms. The constant RTT coefficient equation is an identity over arbitrary coefficient algebras; it does not force commutativity. Any compatible Laurent presentation through an exact faithful monoidal fibre must send the fundamental exchange to a polynomial matrix with polynomial inverse and determinant one. These are necessary conditions. A full noncommutative cocycle, additive translation frame and comparison on every finite comodule remain unconstructed.

statements.title: Cubic elliptic fields on all algebraic jet states
statements.text: For the fixed elliptic two-torsion kernel on the algebraic differential polynomial state space \(P=\operatorname{Sym}(\bigoplus_{m\ge0}\mathfrak{sl}_2^{(m)})\), the local/formal state-field map is constructed through \(\mathbb C[\hbar]/(\hbar^4)\). It retains the original midpoint second-order symbol and \(K=r_0^2/8-r_0^{\prime}/2\), together with the exact admitted normalized all-state cubic exchange. The four-factor and product-pole arguments give actual generating locality with a collision bound independent of spectator polynomial degree and jet orders, and reconstruction gives weak associativity on all polynomial states with independent jets and full outputs. Admitted exchange retains finite meromorphic state span per input, vacuum, shifts, period laws, unitarity and both cubic hexagons. Every admitted skew shift-covariant differential biderivation \(N\), including nonlinear or jet-valued generator outputs, is also realized by \(\delta S_3=N\), \(\delta Y_3=-M_zN/2\). The exact midpoint/endpoint gauge preserves the declared recipients. The whole admitted cubic family keeps that finite-precision scope. The selected scalar-corrected, ordered-state-normalized realization has all-order local formal fields on \(P[[\hbar]]\), agreeing with \(Y_0\) through \(Y_5\) and \(S_0\) through \(S_6\), and a chosen sixth field is separately constructed at precision \(\mathbb C[\hbar]/(\hbar^7)\). Generated supported coefficient operations and the precisely marked KZ instance also exist. The common native category, equality with the chosen sixth field, separately normalized higher moment application and global comparisons remain open. The normalized zero homogeneous exchange correction does not solve the distinct quartic Yang–Baxter equation.

rows.name: Hall algebras and shuffle algebras
rows.summary: Scalar bar–cobar duality determines the exact wheel-supported difference from shuffle algebras, and one-loop Hall currents have a faithful rational realization and dressed spectral coproduct. A state–field correspondence and module comparison must still identify the geometric operations. Critical Hall-to-field comparison retains both branches and the intersection attachment.

statements.title: Scalar bar–cobar duality and wheel defects
statements.text: Let \(k\) be a field of characteristic zero, \(G=\mathbb G_a\) or \(\mathbb G_m\), \(\varepsilon=\pm1\), and \(0\ne\gamma\in\mathcal O(G^2)\), with no nonunit factor depending on only one variable; write \(O_m=\mathcal O(G^m)\), \(\Lambda_m=O_m^{S_m}\), and let a superscript \(S_m,\varepsilon\) mean transformation by \(\varepsilon^{\ell(w)}\), with \(\ell(w)\) the Coxeter length. The coalgebra \(C_{\gamma,m}=(\prod_{i<j}\gamma(Z_i,Z_j))O_m^{S_m,\varepsilon}\), with consecutive-block coproducts, and the quadratic algebra \(B_\gamma=T_k(O_1)/(\gamma O_2^{S_2,\varepsilon})\), with generators in degree one, satisfy \(\Omega C_\gamma\simeq B_\gamma\) and \(C_\gamma\simeq\operatorname{Bar}B_\gamma\) in the category of sequences of \(\Lambda_m\)-modules. If also \(\gamma(Z_1,Z_2)\) and \(\gamma(Z_2,Z_1)\) are coprime, the map from \(B_{\gamma,m}\) to the big shuffle space \(O_m^{S_m,-\varepsilon}\), with unaveraged shuffle kernel \(\gamma(Z_j,Z_i)\) and permutation sign \((-\varepsilon)^{\ell(w)}\), has kernel \(H^0_{W_m}(B_{\gamma,m})\) and cokernel \(H^1_{W_m}(B_{\gamma,m})\), where \(W_m\subset\operatorname{Spec}\Lambda_m\) is the wheel locus. Its image is the shuffle subalgebra generated in weight one, so the map to that smaller algebra is surjective with the same torsion kernel and zero cokernel.
statements.antecedents: Bayer–Sturmfels (1998); Loday–Vallette (2012); Kunin–Lienkaemper–Rosen (2020); Dotsenko–Feigin–Reineke (2021); Dotsenko–Feigin–Kucharski–Reineke (2024); Neguţ (2022).

statements.title: When wheel defects appear
statements.text: Over a field \(k\) of characteristic zero, let \(\gamma\) be a unit times \(g(Z_1-Z_2)\) on \(\mathbb G_a\), or a unit times \(g(Z_1/Z_2)\) on \(\mathbb G_m\), where \(g\ne0\), \(g(0)\ne0\) in the multiplicative case, and \(\gamma(Z_1,Z_2)\) is coprime to its reverse; either exchange sign \(\varepsilon=\pm1\) is allowed. Over an algebraic closure, let \(r\) be the least length of a root sequence of \(g\), with repetitions allowed, whose sum is zero in the additive case or whose product is one in the multiplicative case; set \(r=\infty\) if there is none. Then \(r\ge3\), both wheel-supported defects of the quadratic-to-shuffle comparison vanish in weights \(m<r\), and both are nonzero in every weight \(m\ge r\). If \(r<\infty\), the weight-one-generated shuffle algebra is neither quadratic nor Koszul for its weight grading.

statements.title: One-loop Hall currents and their coproduct
statements.text: Over \(R=\mathbb Q[\eta]\), take the zero-potential one-loop Hall algebra \(B=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]^{S_n}\), with loop weight \(-\eta\), first input the subrepresentation, no rank shift and unaveraged shuffle kernel \((v+\eta)/v\). Its Cartan extension \(A=B\rtimes R[p_0,p_1,\ldots]\), where \(p_r\) acts on weight \(n\) by multiplication by \(\sum_{i=1}^n x_i^r\), is faithfully realized by rational creation and occupation currents over the family of all finite sets of algebraically independent sites. Cartan dressing gives a unital algebra map \(\Delta_z:A\to(A\otimes_RA)((z^{-1}))\), conjugate to separation of the sites, with \((\varepsilon\otimes1)\Delta_z=\mathrm{id}\), \((1\otimes\varepsilon)\Delta_z=e^{zT}\) and shifted coassociativity: for three blocks at \((x+z+w,y+w,t)\), compose rationally and then expand at \(w=\infty\), followed coefficientwise by \(z=\infty\). The comparison holds at \(\eta=0\) as well as at nonzero parameters, and joint faithfulness uses the whole family of finite site sets.
statements.antecedents: Kontsevich–Soibelman (2011); Tsymbaliuk (2021); Maillet–Sánchez de Santos (2000); Latyntsev (2021); Jindal–Kaubrys–Latyntsev (2026).

statements.title: From Hall currents to chiral fields
statements.text: For the zero-potential one-loop quiver over \(\mathbb Q[\eta]\), construct a state–field correspondence on a carrier supporting collision maps, and compare its operations with Hall convolution and the Cartan-dressed spectral coproduct. Prove the resulting comparison on module categories, including the pairing kernel that produces exchange. For general quivers and elliptic kernels, determine the coefficient lattices and support conditions needed for analogous constructions.

rows.name: Celestial algebras of self-dual gauge theory
rows.summary: The tree-level two-tower current theory has graded algebraic duality and principal-parts operations, with a quantum construction in the stated finite twistor-degree truncation. Full quantum smooth-module duality, independently defined bulk operations and global state/sewing comparisons remain open.
