statements.title: Tree-level graded duality
statements.text: Let \(\mathfrak g\) be a finite-dimensional simple complex Lie algebra and \(\mathfrak a=\mathfrak g\otimes\mathbb C[v_1,v_2,\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2)\), with \(\epsilon\) even, so the second current tower is an abelian adjoint module. The universal level-zero current vertex algebra \(V(\mathfrak a)\) has polynomial ghost algebra \(B_{\mathrm{pol}}=C_*(\mathfrak a[t])^{\vee_{\mathrm{fib},t}}\), using the restricted dual in polynomial fibre degree and \(t\)-degree, with \(Qc^i=-\tfrac12f_{jk}{}^ic^jc^k\). There is a graded algebraic identification \(B_{\mathrm{pol}}\simeq(\operatorname{Bar}U(\mathfrak a[t]))^{\vee_{\mathrm{fib},t}}\); cobar recovers \(U(\mathfrak a[t])\), whose primitives and \(d/dt\) recover the current conformal algebra and then \(V(\mathfrak a)\). The coefficients are polynomial in ghosts and jets; full energy-homogeneous coefficient cochains and completed smooth duals have different carriers.

statements.title: A flat quantum quotient in four twistor degrees
statements.text: Let \(\mathfrak g\) be finite-dimensional and simple over \(\mathbb C\), normalize its invariant form \(K\) by long-root squared length two, and choose \(a,\ell\in\mathbb C\) satisfying \(2a\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathrm{ad}}((\operatorname{ad}X)^4)=3\ell^2K(X,X)^2\) for every \(X\in\mathfrak g\). Over \(R=\mathbb C[s]/(s^3)\), with \(e_1=(1,0)\), \(e_2=(0,1)\), retain currents \(J[0],J[e_1],J[e_2],J[e_1+e_2],\widetilde J[0]\) and axions \(E[e_1],E[e_2],E[e_1+e_2],F[0]\), assign \(J[\alpha],E[\alpha]\) twistor degree \(\alpha\) and \(\widetilde J[\alpha],F[\alpha]\) degree \(\alpha+e_1+e_2\), and kill every state of total degree outside \(\{0,e_1,e_2,e_1+e_2\}\). This quotient admits an \(R\)-free one-loop vertex deformation with quadratic current coefficient \(s^2a\), linear coefficients \(-s^2h^\vee a/3\), \(-2s^2h^\vee a/3\), axion coupling \(s\ell\), and an explicit differential ghost vertex algebra, both free on their retained ordered derivative monomials. Their pairing \(I\) satisfies \(QI+\tfrac12I_{(0)}I=D_{\mathrm{tot}}H\) for an explicit \(H\), so \(Q+I_{(0)}\) squares to zero on the ghost algebra tensored with every ordinary untwisted module of this quotient; the coupling is Maurer–Cartan modulo total translation.
statements.antecedents: Costello–Paquette (2022); Fernández–Paquette (2024); De Sole–Kac (2005); Gui–Li–Zeng (2022); Li (2016).

statements.title: Algebraic co-vacuum endomorphisms and the missing vacuum fibre
statements.text: Over \(\mathbb C\), let \(\mathfrak g\) be finite-dimensional and simple, \(\mathfrak a=\mathfrak g\otimes\mathbb C[u,v,\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2)\) with \(\epsilon\) even, \(A=U(\mathfrak a[t,t^{-1}])\), \(\mathfrak p=\mathfrak a[t]\), and \(\mathfrak n=t^{-1}\mathfrak a[t^{-1}]\). Form the level-zero vacuum \(V=A\otimes_{U(\mathfrak p)}\mathbb C\) and co-vacuum \(W=A\otimes_{U(\mathfrak n)}\mathbb C\), inducing from the trivial modules, and compute derived Hom in all algebraic left \(A\)-modules with full algebraic cochains and product totalization. Then \(H^0\operatorname{REnd}_A(W)=U(\mathfrak a)^{\mathrm{op}}\), and \(\mathfrak a^*\) embeds as a split vector-space summand of \(H^1\operatorname{REnd}_A(W)\). Moreover, \(\operatorname{RHom}_A(W,V)=0\), whereas \(\mathbb C\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{U(\mathfrak n)}V\simeq\mathbb C\).

statements.title: Divergence of the unrenormalized ghost pairing
statements.text: For the level-zero two-tower gauge current algebra \(\mathfrak g\otimes\mathbb C[v_1,v_2,\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2)\), with \(\mathfrak g\) finite-dimensional simple over \(\mathbb C\) and \(\epsilon\) even, use the vacuum polarization and normalize \(K\) by long-root squared length two. At total polynomial fibre-degree cutoff \(N\), the determinant cocycle on mode numbers \(m,-m\) of the constant currents is \(2h^\vee(N+1)(N+2)mK_{ab}\). It has no finite limit when \(mK_{ab}\ne0\), so this unrenormalized vacuum construction supplies no finite complementary-level ghost pairing.

statements.title: Completed and quantum celestial duality
statements.text: For the two adjoint towers of a simple complex gauge Lie algebra, construct a completion and localization that compare smooth celestial modules with a curved or differential ghost dual, retaining the vacuum and all polynomial fibre degrees. Extend the quantum current and ghost construction beyond the four-degree quotient, and compare its collision operations with the local observables of an independently quantized self-dual gauge theory on twistor space. A finite-on-input principal-parts operator must be promoted to an algebra-valued operation on the chosen completed carrier before it can define the required coproduct and module tensor product.

rows.name: Celestial self-dual gravity and the Moyal deformation
rows.summary: Polynomial Hamiltonian currents have algebraic duality and formal Moyal constructions. Exact Hessian and strict-source obstructions constrain their stated comparison classes while leaving essential higher source operations possible. Smooth quantum duality, continuous product-and-bracket compatibility and global bulk realization remain separate targets.

statements.title: Tree-level algebraic duality
statements.text: Over \(\mathbb C\), let \(R=\mathbb C[v_1,v_2]\) with \(\{f,g\}=\partial_1f\,\partial_2g-\partial_2f\,\partial_1g\), and let \(\mathfrak a=(R,\{\ ,\ \})\otimes\mathbb C[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2)\), with even \(\epsilon\) and both constant Hamiltonians retained. The universal level-zero current vertex algebra is \(V(\mathfrak a)=U(\mathfrak a[t,t^{-1}])\otimes_{U(\mathfrak a[t])}\mathbb C\); its polynomial ghost algebra is the dual of the homological Chevalley–Eilenberg coalgebra of \(\mathfrak a[t]\), restricted jointly by the shifted fibre degree \(\deg(v^\alpha)=\alpha-(1,1)\) and \(t\)-degree, and is quasi-isomorphic to the corresponding restricted dual of \(\operatorname{Bar}U(\mathfrak a[t])\). The cobar of that coalgebra recovers \(U(\mathfrak a[t])\), whose primitives and translation recover \(V(\mathfrak a)\).

statements.title: An obstruction beyond local cochains
statements.text: Let \(S=\mathbb C[v_1,v_2,z,z^{-1}]\) carry the Poisson bracket in \(v_1,v_2\), and give \(S\) its adjoint module structure over \(\mathfrak h=(S,\{\ ,\ \})\). With \(\mathrm{vol}=dv_1\wedge dv_2\wedge dz\), \(\partial^1=\partial_2\), \(\partial^2=-\partial_1\), and \(J_f=(\partial^a\partial_bf)\), define \(\iota_{\psi(f,g)}\mathrm{vol}=\operatorname{tr}(dJ_f\wedge dJ_g)\) and \(\Phi(f,Y)=\sum_{a,b=1}^2\partial_a\partial^b\bigl(Y(\partial^a\partial_bf)\bigr)\). The cocycle \(\Omega_H(f,g,h)=\Phi(f,\psi(g,h))+\Phi(g,\psi(h,f))+\Phi(h,\psi(f,g))\) represents a nonzero class in \(H^3(\mathfrak h;S)\) computed with all algebraic cochains. No algebraic two-cochain has differential equal to this cocycle.

statements.title: Polynomial Moyal cochains are not closed
statements.text: For polynomial functions on \(\mathbb C^2\), set \(f*_hg=m\exp(\tfrac h2(\partial_1\otimes\partial_2-\partial_2\otimes\partial_1))(f\otimes g)\) and \(b_h(f,g)=(f*_hg-g*_hf)/h\). At every fixed \(h\in\mathbb C^\times\), the finite-polynomial ghost dual is not preserved by the Chevalley–Eilenberg differential: the constant coefficient of \(b_h(v_1^{2r+1},v_2^{2r+1})\) is \((2r+1)!h^{2r}/2^{2r}\) for every \(r\ge0\). The homological Chevalley–Eilenberg coalgebra remains defined, and \(h\)-adic cochains provide the formal dual.

statements.title: Quantum smooth modules and the physical comparison
statements.text: For the universal Hamiltonian current algebra over \(\mathbb C\) and, separately, its \(h\)-adic Moyal deformation or specialization at fixed \(h\in\mathbb C^\times\), construct a completed dual and an equivalence for discrete smooth modules, with common domains for collision operations and exchange. Extend the classical twist on an affine twistor chart to a global comparison with an independently quantized bulk theory, keeping the graviton and axion contributions to the quantum brackets separate.

rows.name: D3 branes and Hilbert-scheme vertex algebras
rows.summary: At every rank the boundary BRST algebra is an exact odd-zero-mode kernel in the specified numerical Hilbert-scheme sections. Formal sheaf cohomology has its sharp range and determinant torsion. Completed finite-rank smooth duality, collision fusion and the independent bulk/defect map remain to be constructed.

statements.title: The boundary algebra is a proper kernel
statements.text: Over \(\mathbb C\), for every integer \(N\ge1\), let \(C_{\mathrm{fr}}\) be the polynomial relative \(\mathfrak{gl}_N\) BRST complex with adjoint and fundamental symplectic bosons and fundamental fermions at numerical \(\hbar=1\), and let \(\mathcal D\) be the corresponding Arakawa–Kuwabara–Möller formal vertex sheaf on \(M_N=\operatorname{Hilb}^N(\mathbb C^2)\). Put \(K_N=H^0(C_{\mathrm{fr}})\) and \(V_N=\Gamma(M_N,\mathcal D)_{\mathrm{fin}}/(\hbar-1)\), taking the torus-finite part before specialization, and write \(\chi^-=\phi\gamma\) for the invariant contraction of a fundamental fermion with a fundamental symplectic boson. The natural map identifies \(K_N\) with \(\ker(\chi^-_{(0)}:V_N\to V_N)\), and \(V_N=K_N\oplus\tau_{(-1)}K_N\) as graded vector spaces, where \(\tau\) is an odd global section of conformal weight zero with \(\chi^-_{(0)}\tau=N\).

statements.title: The sharp formal cohomology range
statements.text: For every integer \(N\ge1\), let \(\mathcal D\) be the \(\mathbb C[[\hbar]]\)-complete Arakawa–Kuwabara–Möller vertex sheaf on \(M_N=\operatorname{Hilb}^N(\mathbb C^2)\). For each of \(\mathcal D\), every quotient \(\mathcal D/\hbar^m\mathcal D\) with integer \(m\ge1\), and the classical quotient \(\mathcal D/\hbar\mathcal D\), its sheaf cohomology is nonzero exactly in degrees \(0\le k<N\). These groups are taken before numerical specialization.

statements.title: An exact determinant-torsion algebra
statements.text: For \(N\ge2\), on \(M_N=\operatorname{Hilb}^N(\mathbb C^2)\), let \(\mathcal D\) be the Arakawa–Kuwabara–Möller formal vertex sheaf over \(R=\mathbb C[[\hbar]]\), let \(\beta\) be the connecting map for \(0\to\mathcal D\xrightarrow{\hbar}\mathcal D\to\mathcal D/\hbar\mathcal D\to0\), and put \(\kappa_r=T^r\beta(\phi\psi)\), where \(\phi\psi\) is the classical invariant contraction of the two fundamental fermions. The normal-cup subalgebra generated by the scalar vacuum and the \(\kappa_r\), using finite sums and finite products, is \[\frac{R\otimes_{\mathbb C}\Lambda(e_0,e_1,\ldots)}{(\hbar e_r\ (r\ge0),\ \Lambda^{\ge N})},\qquad e_r\mapsto\kappa_r.\] Each \(e_r\) has sheaf degree one, intrinsic even parity and conformal weight \(r+1\); the exterior sign comes from sheaf degree, and there is no completion in the translation index. Every nonempty increasing product of fewer than \(N\) generators is nonzero and not \(\hbar\)-divisible, remains nonzero in every finite \(\hbar\)-quotient, and vanishes under torus-finite specialization at \(\hbar=1\).

statements.title: A completed D3 duality and bulk map
statements.text: Over \(\mathbb C\), for the boundary vertex algebras at every finite rank \(N\ge1\) and their polynomial rank-parameter family, construct a completed chiral Koszul dual together with a specified category of smooth modules and a functorial equivalence preserving the vacuum and collisions. Compare that construction with independently defined twisted bulk observables and defects, including the normalization of the rank parameter; the classical bar models and the finite-word vacuum-mode algebra do not supply this comparison.

rows.name: M2 branes and the two-matrix algebra
rows.summary: Polynomial transport is established through arity five at every positive rank and through all arities up to rank four. At zero Cherednik coupling and a fixed nonzero complex Weyl parameter, ordinary derived modules over the finite-particle cohomology algebra correspond to equivariant curved coderived comodules and contraderived contramodules; algebraic sewing has nonzero derived corrections. All-rank all-arity transport with its integral parameter and the independent five-dimensional comparison remain open.

statements.title: Polynomial transport without inverting the parameter
statements.text: Let \(N\ge1\), work over \(\mathbb Q[h]\), and give \(L_h=\mathbb Q[x,y][h]\) the divided Moyal bracket \(b_h=(f*_hg-g*_hf)/h\), with \([x,y]_* =h\). Let \(K_N\) be the polynomial \(GL_N\)-invariant quantum two-matrix BRST complex, with \([X_{ij},Y_{kl}]=h\delta_{il}\delta_{jk}\), the moment matrix \(YX-XY+hNI\), antighost degree \(-1\), and \(\operatorname{Tr}\psi=0\), using divided graded commutators in the target. The symmetrized trace \(J(f)=\operatorname{Tr}\operatorname{Sym}f\) extends to polynomial \(L_\infty\) Taylor maps of ghost degree \(1-n\) through arity five on all polynomial inputs, and to all arities when \(1\le N\le4\). At each proved arity, coupling equations use the arity-completed space \(\prod_{n\ge1}\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb Q[h]}(\Lambda^nL_h,K_N)\) with divided convolution bracket; the ordinary associative convention instead uses source bracket \(hb_h\) and Taylor maps multiplied by \(h^{n-1}\).

statements.title: A finite-rank obstruction to derived sewing
statements.text: Over \(\mathbb C\), with algebraic tensor products and ordinary derived functors, fix \(\hbar\ne0\) and \(N\ge1\), let \(W=\mathbb C\langle x,y\rangle/(xy-yx-\hbar)\), \(\mathfrak g=W^{\mathrm{Lie}}\), \(U_N=U(\mathfrak g)/(z-N1)\), where \(z\) denotes the central Lie element \(1_W\), and \(A_N=(W^{\otimes N})^{S_N}\). For the algebraic power-sum map \(U_N\to A_N\), \(J(f)\mapsto\sum_i f^{(i)}\), the multiplication \(A_N\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{U_N}A_N\to A_N\) is never a quasi-isomorphism. The module \(F_N=\mathbb C[x_1,\ldots,x_N]^{S_N}\), with \(y_i=-\hbar\partial_{x_i}\), has no flat first-order lift as the central value varies from \(N\), and its resulting class in \(\operatorname{Ext}^2_{U_N}(F_N,F_N)\) is nonzero. For \(N=1,2\), \(\operatorname{Tor}^{U_N}_1(A_N,A_N)=0\) and \(\operatorname{Tor}^{U_N}_2(A_N,A_N)\ne0\), with the central-extension cap product surjecting onto \(A_N\); for \(N\ge3\), at least one of these two Tor groups is nonzero.
statements.antecedents: Gaiotto–Oh (2019); Etingof (2014); Joseph (1970); Lowen (2004); Pinczon–Ushirobira (2005); Costello (2017).

statements.title: Higher transport and the five-dimensional theory
statements.text: Over \(\mathbb Q[h]\), for every integer \(N\ge1\), extend the polynomial transport from the Moyal Lie algebra to the two-matrix BRST complex to every arity at every rank without inverting \(h\), and determine the permitted changes of its lower Taylor maps. For an independently quantized five-dimensional noncommutative Chern–Simons theory, construct supported bulk, line and surface observables and the maps that compare their products and junctions with this algebraic transport, including the loop parameter, Moyal parameter and rank normalization.

rows.name: M5 branes, Miura algebras and surface fusion
rows.summary: Miura rank addition has an exact coassociative coproduct and Weyl-symbol formula. The first surface correction has the stated conditional reflection result. Identifying quantum surface fusion and mixed line–surface junctions requires an independent defect construction on compatible domains.

statements.title: Miura composition as a Moyal product
statements.text: For positive integers \(N_1,N_2\), take independent Heisenberg currents with \(J_i(z)J_j(w)\sim k\delta_{ij}/(z-w)^2\) over \(\mathbb C[a,k]\), and form the universal Miura images of \(\prod_{i=1}^N(a\partial+J_i)\). If \(\widehat U\) is the Weyl symbol obtained from the normally ordered symbol by \(\exp(-\tfrac a2\partial_z\partial_p)\), the coproduct is \[\widehat U^{(12)}=\widehat U^{(1)}\exp\!\left[\frac a2\left(\overleftarrow\partial_p\overrightarrow\partial_z-\overleftarrow\partial_z\overrightarrow\partial_p\right)\right]\widehat U^{(2)}.\] This is a coassociative, vacuum-preserving vertex-algebra map from rank \(N_1+N_2\) to the tensor product of the two Miura images. After inverting \(k\), its stress tensor has central charge \(c(N)=N-N(N^2-1)a^2/k\).

statements.title: Reflection and the first surface correction
statements.text: Consider one-flavour noncommutative Chern–Simons theory on \(\mathbb R_t\times\mathbb C^2\), with \([z_1,z_2]_* =c_{\mathrm M}\), surface \(t=z_2=0\), fixed classical surface currents, current level and universal or finite-rank boundary condition for the surface algebra, and logarithmic flux odd in the loop parameter \(\hbar\). Assume a perturbative defect quantization exists with coincident-point counterterms compatible with \(t\mapsto-t\), and that its Ward equations are reflection covariant with solutions unique modulo changes that are the identity on the classical currents. Then the first-order surface deformation class vanishes. If the currents and source coupling themselves admit a reflection-equivariant choice, their first-order coefficients vanish in that choice.

statements.title: One comparison for surfaces and junctions
statements.text: For an independently renormalized five-dimensional noncommutative Chern–Simons theory with M5 surface defects, construct the surface coefficient complexes and compare physical surface fusion with the rank-adding Miura coproduct. Construct, on the same domains, the line-fusion and mixed line–surface junction maps and compare them with the shifted affine Yangian operations, retaining their distinct parameters and units.

statements.title: Positive sewing is rigid from a local crossing domain
statements.text: Fix real \(c>1\), \(Q=\sqrt{(c-1)/6}\), principal weights \(h(P)=Q^2/4+P^2\) with \(P>0\), and normalized Virasoro sphere blocks \(F_p^s(x)\), \(F_p^t(x)\). Let \(C:(0,\infty)^3\to(0,\infty)\) be finite, measurable and fully symmetric, and let \(B:(0,\infty)\to(0,\infty)\) be finite measurable; suppose that for almost every external quadruple the two channel integrals, including \[G_s(x)=\int_0^\infty\frac{C(P_1,P_2,p)C(p,P_3,P_4)}{B(p)}\lvert F_p^s(x)\rvert^2\,dp,\] are locally bounded and equal throughout \(\lvert x\rvert<1,\ \lvert1-x\rvert<1\). Then, almost everywhere, \(B=a^2/\rho_0\) and \(C=K\,a(P_1)a(P_2)a(P_3)C_0\), where \(K>0\), \(a=\sqrt{B\rho_0}\), \(C_0\) is the Barnes-normalized three-point coefficient, and \(\rho_0(P)=4\sqrt2\sinh(2\pi bP)\sinh(2\pi P/b)\). Choose \(b+b^{-1}=Q\), with \(0<b\le1\) for \(c\ge25\) and \(b=e^{i\theta}\), \(0<\theta<\pi/2\), for \(1<c<25\).

statements.title: Boundary traces and the vacuum weight
statements.text: Fix real \(c>1\) and assume two positive principal Virasoro actions of weights \(h(P)=(c-1)/24+P^2\) are realized on \(L^2(\mathbb R_+,dP;\operatorname{HS}(\mathcal F))\), where \(\mathcal F\) is the oscillator Fock Hilbert space and the actions are \(L_n\xi=\pi_P(L_n)\xi\), \(\bar L_n\xi=\xi\pi_P(L_{-n})\), with their common finite-energy domain and trace-compatible positive sewing. Their faithful all-temperature state data are parametrized by measurable \(w>0\) almost everywhere with \(\int_0^\infty w(P)e^{-\beta P^2}\,dP<\infty\) for every \(\beta>0\), and have caps \(\Psi^w_\beta(P)=\sqrt{w(P)}e^{-\beta H_P/2}\), where \(H_P=P^2+N-1/24\) and \(N\) is the oscillator number operator on \(\mathcal F\). The Ward identities leave \(w\) free, while equality of the amplitude with the normalized modular vacuum amplitude at every temperature selects \(w=\rho_0\) almost everywhere. Here \(\rho_0(P)=2\sqrt2[\cosh(2\pi QP)-\cosh(2\pi\widehat QP)]\), \(Q=\sqrt{(c-1)/6}\), \(\widehat Q^2=Q^2-4\).

statements.title: Preparing a gravitational state from the bulk
statements.text: Construct regulated half-solid-torus integrals for real three-dimensional Einstein gravity in a fixed asymptotically anti-de Sitter solid-torus sector, with an invertible real coframe, Brown–Henneaux boundary conditions and a fixed boundary map, whose mixed pairings converge as both regulators are removed independently. Prove that the resulting vectors satisfy the Virasoro Ward identities, temperature evolution and physical sewing, have the normalized modular vacuum amplitude, and use the same stress charge as the local bulk action. This requires an independently defined gravitational integral and its comparison with the boundary representation.

statements.title: Finite normal words and independent-height primitive limits
statements.text:
Ordinary and first-normal boundary insertions cover every fixed finite word in the universal \(e,h,f,b,c\) source through bare orders zero and one, with its actual source differential. Independent-height ordinary and first-normal one-vertex \(u,h\) primitives have boundary and fixed-positive-height interior extensions, with their exact spatial contacts. Selected same-root second-normal rows retain their grouped Ward and reference-scale heat limits. The coincident finite PBW conversion has zero fixed normal projection with its full Hom companion retained.

Scope: Fix every source, field, component, jet and derivative stage; no estimate is uniform as those stages grow. Boundary finite words use one height derivative before zero-height restriction, compact simultaneous tangential ratios, compact positive running scales and the separately specified source normal-contact extensions. The independent-height theorem covers the one-vertex \(u,h\) matrix and its ordered \(h,s\) spectators in \(a\le a_0<\min(1,\sqrt{L_0}/16)\), with upper heat time \(L\in[L_0,L_1]\subset(0,\infty)\). Here \(r_\pm\ge0\) are root heights, \(d\) is tangential separation and \(a^2=(r_++r_-)^2+2|d|^2\). Its boundary estimate has no restriction on height, separation or cutoff ratios. Only the separated zero-lower-source representation requires \(0<\sqrt\epsilon\le b/8\), with \(b^2=(r_+-r_-)^2+2|d|^2\). The interior constant may depend on the positive mean height. The second-normal theorem retains its selected zero-jet, field-number-three rows; higher incoming normal tree and unary constructions have their own finite-moment normalization.

rows.name: Arithmetic: Weil positivity, spectral duality and integral jets
rows.summary: Continuous spectral duality, integral normal/Frobenius coefficients and a trace representative of the full Weil functional are established. The positive critical multiplicity layers retain an exact nonreal remainder, and the counting trace differs from a cyclic vector state. Full positivity and native field, operation and state realization remain open.

statements.title: A continuous spectral dual retaining multiplicities
statements.text: Over \(\mathbb C\), let \(S_{00}=\{\phi\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R)^{\mathrm{even}}:\phi(0)=\int\phi=0\}\) with its Schwartz topology, let \(E_n=\{f:e^{n\sqrt{1+x^2}}f\in H^n(\mathbb R)\}\) with norm \(\|e^{n\sqrt{1+x^2}}f\|_{H^n}\), and give \(E=\bigcap_{n\ge2}E_n\) its projective-limit Fréchet topology. The integer-summation map \(Z\phi(x)=2\sum_{m\ge1}\phi(me^x)\) is a continuous embedding with closed image, so the complex \([S_{00}\xrightarrow{Z}E]\), in degrees zero and one, has only \(H^1=M=E/Z(S_{00})\). For \(\xi(s)=\tfrac12s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)\), let \(m_\rho\) be the order of its zero \(\rho\) and set \(V_n=\overline{\operatorname{span}\{x^ke^{\rho x}/k!:0\le k<m_\rho\}}^{\,E_n'}\); the strong continuous dual of \(M\), twisted by the dilation character \(e^t\), is topologically \((\operatorname{ind\,lim}_nV_n)\otimes\mathbb C(1)\), with nondegenerate evaluation pairing into the character line \(\mathbb C(1)\). For the dilation generator \(\Theta_M[f]=[-f']\), each zero contributes its full Jordan block of length \(m_\rho\); neither the Riemann hypothesis nor simplicity of zeros is assumed.
statements.antecedents: Riemann (1859); Connes (1999); Meyer (2004, 2005); Paugam (2009); Fesenko–Ricotta–Suzuki (2012); Andreotti–Kas (1973).

statements.title: Integral arithmetic translations retain normal directions
statements.text: Fix a prime \(p\), a depth \(r\ge1\), and the category of \(p\)-complete, \(p\)-torsion-free \(\delta\)-algebras over \(\mathbb Z_p\), with Frobenius equal to the identity on \(\mathbb Z_p\); all completions below are \(p\)-adic, and profinite labels are interpreted through the constant profinite formal scheme, allowing variation on idempotent components. Put \(R=\mathbb Z_p[x_0,x_1,\ldots]^\wedge_p\), \(\varphi(x_i)=x_i^p+px_{i+1}\), and \(H_r=(\Gamma_{\mathbb Z_p}(t_0,\ldots,t_{r-2})\otimes\mathbb Z_p[w_0,w_1,\ldots])^\wedge_p\), where \(\Gamma\) denotes a divided-power algebra, its generator list is empty at \(r=1\), and \(H_r\) represents on each test algebra \(T\) displacements \(v\) satisfying \(\delta^i(v)\in pT\) for \(i<r\), with \(\delta^i(v)=pt_i\) and \(t_{r-1}=w_0\). Writing \(C(\mathbb Z_p,\mathbb Z_p)\) for continuous functions, the map \(R\hookrightarrow C(\mathbb Z_p,\mathbb Z_p)\widehat\otimes H_r\), \(f\mapsto[(a,v)\mapsto f(a+v)]\), is injective and intertwines finite-weight normal convolution; it extends to comparison maps of the entire congruence-groupoid nerve, whose enriched objects are \((a,v)\) and arrows exist when \(a\equiv b\pmod{p^r}\), compatibly with every composition, depth reduction and coefficient reduction, with Frobenius compatibility after twisting the source action by \(\varphi\). For \(r\ge2\), the relation \(\varphi(x_0)-x_0\) vanishes on arithmetic points but its normal coefficient \([t_0]\) is \(-p\), so point evaluation cannot retain this action modulo \(p^2\).
statements.antecedents: Joyal (1985); Buium (1996, 2000); Buium–Ralph–Simanca (2011); Bhatt–Scholze (2022); Bertapelle–Previato–Saha (2023); Cartier (1955–1956).

statements.title: Positivity on arbitrary compact intervals
statements.text: For the complete Weil quadratic form \(Q\) of the Riemann zeta function, prove \(Q(g)\ge0\) for every compactly supported complex \(g\in L^2(\mathbb R)\), interpreting the value outside the finite-energy domain as \(+\infty\). The finite support-length bound does not provide this unbounded family of inequalities. The finite-matrix criterion retains the complete residual and tail terms. Fourier and Schur reductions do not establish the required signed bounds at every window.

statements.title: Arithmetic fields and their trace comparison
statements.text: At a fixed prime \(p\), construct an integral ordered collision system and a trace/evaluation comparison on the arithmetic normal carrier, preserving both endpoint actions, the unit, Frobenius and all collision compositions. The comparison must detect the nonzero normal class modulo \(p^2\), retain ternary compatibility and admit a global arithmetic realization without discarding the integral coefficient lattice.

rows.name: K3 surfaces, compact Hall theory and the Igusa form
rows.summary: Specified strong orientation, local reduced mixed/ordinary flags and numerical modular formulas are available. The proposed BPS and minimal Gritsenko–Nikulin sources have different imaginary parity spaces. Global compact reduction, actual primitive recognition, untraced protected states and the geometric modular line/section comparison remain to be constructed.

statements.title: Strong orientation on two compact component classes
statements.text: Over \(\mathbb C\), let \(S\) be a smooth projective Kummer K3 surface, \(E\) an elliptic curve and \(X=S\times E\), with a fixed Calabi–Yau volume form and induced trivial spin structure; choose a smooth elliptic fibre \(C\subset S\), a divisor \(D\) with \(D\cdot C=1\), points \(p\in C\), \(x\in E\), and \(L\in\operatorname{Pic}^0(E)\). In the actual component group \(K_0^{\mathrm{semi}}(X)\) of perfect complexes, let \(\Gamma\) be generated by \(\alpha=[\mathcal O_C\boxtimes\mathcal O_x]\) and \(\beta=[\mathcal O_p\boxtimes L]\), and restrict a Joyce–Upmeier square root \(J_F^{\otimes2}\simeq\det R\operatorname{Hom}_X(F,F)\), compatible with direct sums and equipped with a square-compatible unit, to these components. Then \(\Gamma\simeq\mathbb Z^2\), its Euler pairing is zero, and \(J\) admits associative unital square-compatible maps \(J_F\otimes J_G\otimes\det R\operatorname{Hom}_X(F,G)\simeq J_{F\oplus G}\), extending to every actual finite ordered filtration whose successive quotient classes lie in \(\Gamma\), independently of binary parenthesization and compatibly with refinements. For the fixed root, enhancement classes form a two-element torsor under \(H^2(\Gamma,\mathbb F_2)\).

statements.title: The numerical reduced Igusa formula
statements.text: Let \(S\) be a smooth projective complex K3 surface, \(E\) an elliptic curve, \(\beta\ne0\) an effective integral curve class on \(S\), \(d\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\), and \(n\in\mathbb Z\); use reduced Donaldson–Thomas invariants of \(S\times E\) defined by the translation quotient with finite stabilizers, rational stabilizer weights and the Behrend-weighted sign convention. With \(c(a,b,m)=[q^ap^by^m]\chi_{10}(y,q,p)^{-1}\) for the product-normalized Igusa cusp form, the numerical identity is \[\mathrm{DT}^{S\times E,\mathrm{red}}_{n,(\beta,d)}=(-1)^{n+1}\sum_{\substack{r>0,\ r\mid n\\ \beta/r\ \mathrm{integral}}}\frac1r\,c\!\left(\frac{(\beta/r)^2}{2},d-1,\frac nr\right).\] This includes imprimitive \(\beta\) through the displayed divisor sum and determines numerical invariants, without determining the parity-resolved BPS spaces or their brackets.
statements.cite: Georg Oberdieck, “Multiple cover formulas for K3 geometries, wall-crossing, and Quot schemes”, Geometry & Topology 28 (2024), Theorem 1.5; Georg Oberdieck and Junliang Shen, “Reduced Donaldson–Thomas invariants and the ring of dual numbers”, Proceedings of the London Mathematical Society 118 (2019).

statements.title: From compact Hall operations to an automorphic state
statements.text: On \(S\times E\), with \(S\) a smooth projective Kummer K3 surface and \(E\) an elliptic curve, take the actual component lattice generated by \(\mathcal O_C\boxtimes\mathcal O_x\) and \(\mathcal O_p\boxtimes L\), where \(C\subset S\) is a smooth elliptic fibre, a divisor meets \(C\) once, \(p\in C\), \(x\in E\), and \(L\in\operatorname{Pic}^0(E)\). Construct translation-equivariant descent of strong orientation and a comparison of reduced compact critical coefficients that preserves extension products and every actual ordered flag refinement, including the orientation-ratio torsor and relative translation data. Determine the resulting primitive algebra and whether a cyclic state with the normalized inverse-Igusa series can be prepared from these operations.

Correct boundary comparisons, further geometric hypotheses and state/sewing constructions remain separate problems.

statements.title: Negative-current homology obstructs preservation of the tensor unit
statements.text: Over \(\mathbb C\), let \(A=L_1(\mathfrak{psl}(2|2))\) be the simple affine boundary algebra with its even \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) factors at levels \(-1,+1\), let \(\mathfrak g=A_1\) be its weight-one current space, and let \(\mathfrak n_-=t^{-1}\mathfrak g[t^{-1}]\) act by the actual negative current modes. In the ordinary algebraic derived category, \(F_-(A)=\mathbb C\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{U(\mathfrak n_-)}A\) has \(H_{0,0}=\mathbb C\) and \(H_{1,2}=\mathbb C^{24\mid24}\), with every other group of conformal weight at most two zero; the indices denote homological degree and conformal weight. Consequently \(F_-\) cannot be strong unital monoidal from a tensor category with unit \(A\) to complexes of vector spaces with their ordinary tensor product.

statements.title: The ordinary dual of the graded surface singularity
statements.text: Over \(\mathbb C\), give \(Z=\mathbb C[u,v,w]/(uv-w^2)\) cohomological degrees \(|u|=|v|=|w|=2\), zero differential and augmentation at the singular point, and use the ordinary unbounded dg-module category with full derived Hom. Its derived augmentation endomorphism algebra is formal and is \(U(\mathfrak l)\) with zero differential, where \(\mathfrak l\) has generators \(\alpha,\beta,\gamma\) of degree \(-1\), a central generator \(\tau\) of degree \(-2\), brackets \([\alpha,\beta]=-\tau\), \([\gamma,\gamma]=2\tau\), and all other generator brackets zero up to graded skewsymmetry. Every generator is primitive, and \(R\operatorname{Hom}_{U(\mathfrak l)}(\mathbb C,\mathbb C)\simeq Z\) multiplicatively; this duality has no extra spectral parameter.

statements.title: The geometric premise and sheaf invariants of the six-sphere families
statements.text: Determine whether the proposed \((3,4,\infty)\) modular torus fibration with logarithmic-transform twists \((0,1,-1)\), its finite quotient fillings and toric cusp gluing defines a smooth compact complex threefold with underlying smooth manifold \(S^6\). Conditional on these geometric construction hypotheses and those of the Liu–Rollenske family, compare their actual Dolbeault and chiral de Rham cohomology, including the connecting maps needed beyond numerical indices.

statements.title: Induced vacuum pairing vanishes at zero extension
statements.text: For \(n=2,3\) and a nonzero finite-dimensional complex Lie algebra \(\mathfrak g\), use the polynomial punctured-space current model \(L_n\), its regular subalgebra \(P_n\) and negative subalgebra \(N_n\), at zero central extension. In the ordinary algebraic derived category put \(W_n=U(L_n)\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{U(N_n)}\mathbb C\) and \(V_n=U(L_n)\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{U(P_n)}\mathbb C\). For both full Hom and internally graded Hom, \[R\operatorname{Hom}_{U(L_n)}(W_n,V_n)=0,\qquad \mathbb C\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{U(N_n)}\operatorname{Res}_{N_n}V_n\simeq\mathbb C.\] At \(\mathfrak g=0\), the derived Hom is \(\mathbb C\), so the nonzero hypothesis is essential.

statements.title: The higher-current endomorphism algebra
statements.text: For any finite-dimensional complex Lie algebra \(\mathfrak g\), use the polynomial punctured-space current model at zero central extension and \(W_n=U(L_n)\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{U(N_n)}\mathbb C\), in ordinary algebraic derived modules. In complex dimension two, its derived endomorphism dg algebra is formal for either full or internally graded Hom, although its general nonabelian multiplication is not computed. In dimension three the internally graded cohomology algebra is \[H^*R\operatorname{End}_{\mathrm{gr}}(W_3)\cong U(P_3)\ltimes\Lambda(N_3^\vee[-1]),\] where \(\vee\) is the restricted internal-weight dual, the exterior generators have degree \(-1\), and the action is \(\rho^\vee(p)\lambda=-\lambda\circ\rho(p)\), with \(\rho(x\otimes f)(y\otimes t)=[x,y]\otimes ft\) using truncated multiplication on principal parts. Before the antipode converts right multiplication, degree zero is canonically \(U(P_3)^{\mathrm{op}}\); formality in dimension three is open.

statements.title: From the quantum obstruction to a defect algebra
statements.text: For a cyclic holomorphic Chern–Simons theory on \(\mathbb C^3\) with its standard holomorphic volume form and a chosen curve defect, construct the cyclic open-string dg or \(A_\infty\) algebra, the coupling to transverse jets and a morphism from the local field-theory deformation complex to the defect deformation complex. The morphism must preserve the deformation degree and carry the first quantum master-equation obstruction to the first obstruction to the defect operations, with any cancellation supplied by an explicitly coupled field. Construct compatible higher configuration operations and nonzero-extension induced objects on the same coefficient and completion spaces.

statements.title: Cubic compatibility for full retained-point current morphisms
statements.text: For invariant cubic current systems on a complex surface, let \(A\) be the prescribed unary map and let \(\ell\theta\), \(\ell^{\prime}\theta^{\prime}\) be the central cubic tensors. A filtered vacuum-preserving morphism of the full retained-point systems exists exactly when \(A\) is a Lie map and \(\ell\theta=\ell^{\prime}A^*\theta^{\prime}\). The system retains collisions, vacant-position maps, permutations, partitions, and their mixed coherences. The map \(\operatorname{Sym}(A)\) supplies a full morphism when these conditions hold. Lower correction terms have the stated differential image, while full morphisms between fixed invariant-cubic fibres have zero supported residual. Finite stages bound total particle, central, and Koszul weight together. An independent mixed bulk, a singular-field realization, and an automorphism classification require further constructions.

statements.title: Finite-jet cubic currents in free elliptic reduction
statements.text: In free elliptic reduction on the fixed six-field carrier, confined cubic distributional limits, the central de Rham primitive and raw eight-face cube lift remain. The specified one-lower-row incoming \(\eta/s\) relation module now admits arbitrary finite independent holomorphic right state jets, all anchors and fixed smooth joint coefficients, retaining the actual coefficient differential. The third Green-pair derivatives are transferred by \(\partial_U+\partial_V\) before the annular estimates. Separate marked-object rows give the all-top \(s\) and bare \(\eta\) source equations and all joint faces at this scope. Critical moments are signed, and high compact-anchor jets still need integration by parts rather than a universal absolute-moment bound. The canonical cubic cone and contraction at every defined contact order are available from the specified source. All sixteen histories now exist on the specified polynomial-Thom carrier, with the first transverse projection and the fresh-normal-degree-zero supported partner on its admitted finite old jets. The full relative comparison still requires the original fixed current recipient, its complete generated history and incidence diagram, the remaining after-contact applications and coefficient boundaries, compact endpoint and independent arrows with the lower marking held fixed. Exactness in the full de Rham carrier does not imply exactness in the smaller supported Dolbeault complex.
